title: Remote Specialist Treatment Planning in Paediatric Dentistry: A Qualitative Evaluation and Refinement of a Web-Based Prototype
abstract: Abstract Background Access to specialist paediatric dental expertise is unevenly distributed, which may limit opportunities for specialist input into treatment planning for children requiring dental general anaesthesia (DGA). Digital approaches may provide a mechanism for remote specialist case review, however, the feasibility, usability, and acceptability of remote specialist treatment planning in paediatric dentistry remain uncertain. This study aimed to explore specialists’ experiences of using a prototype web-based platform for remote treatment planning and to identify refinements required before further evaluation. Methods Specialists in paediatric dentistry used a prototype web-based platform to remotely review and treatment plan paediatric cases using radiographs, intra-oral photographs, and structured clinical information, and subsequently participated in a semi-structured focus group. Data were analysed using a pragmatic qualitative approach. Findings were organised deductively according to four predefined domains; feasibility, usability, acceptability, and implementation, with more granular subthemes developed inductively within these domains. Results Three specialists in paediatric dentistry participated in the focus group. Remote specialist treatment planning was considered potentially feasible when sufficient, appropriately presented diagnostic information was available. Participants identified image quality and completeness, clarity of the digital workflow, technical reliability, and appropriate onboarding as important influences on confidence in using the platform. Participants expressed positive views regarding the potential value of remote specialist input, particularly where access to specialist expertise is limited. Future implementation was considered dependent on preserving professional judgement within a structured treatment-planning process and providing clear information regarding the use of clinical data. Conclusion Remote specialist treatment planning using a web-based platform was perceived as potentially feasible and valuable by the specialists participating in this study, but its successful implementation was considered dependent on the quality of diagnostic information, usability and reliability of the digital workflow, appropriate user preparation, and preservation of professional judgement. These findings informed refinement of the prototype and provide a basis for subsequent evaluation of the reliability and clinical utility of remote specialist treatment planning in paediatric dentistry.

Data were analysed using a pragmatic qualitative approach. Findings were organised deductively according to four predefined domains; feasibility, usability, acceptability, and implementation, with more granular subthemes developed inductively within these domains. Results Three specialists in paediatric dentistry participated in the focus group. Remote specialist treatment planning was considered potentially feasible when sufficient, appropriately presented diagnostic information was available. Participants identified image quality and completeness, clarity of the digital workflow, technical reliability, and appropriate onboarding as important influences on confidence in using the platform. Participants expressed positive views regarding the potential value of remote specialist input, particularly where access to specialist expertise is limited. Future implementation was considered dependent on preserving professional judgement within a structured treatment-planning process and providing clear information regarding the use of clinical data. Conclusion Remote specialist treatment planning using a web-based platform was perceived as potentially feasible and valuable by the specialists participating in this study, but its successful implementation was considered dependent on the quality of diagnostic information, usability and reliability of the digital workflow, appropriate user preparation, and preservation of professional judgement. These findings informed refinement of the prototype and provide a basis for subsequent evaluation of the reliability and clinical utility of remote specialist treatment planning in paediatric dentistry.

title: Time to initiation of Antenatal care and its predictors among pastoral pregnant women in madawalabu district public health facilities, southeastern Ethiopia, 2024: retrospective follow-up study
abstract: Abstract Background: Timely initiation of antenatal care within the first trimester is critical for reducing maternal morbidity and mortality through early detection of complications and provision of key preventive interventions. Pastoralist communities, however, face substantial geographic and sociocultural barriers that may delay antennal care initiation, and empirical evidence on these determinants remains limited. Objective: To assess time to initiation of antenatal care and its predictors among pastoral pregnant women in Madawalabu district, southeastern Ethiopia. Methods: A facility‑based retrospective follow‑up study was conducted among 475 pregnant women who received antenatal care services at public health facilities in Madawalabu district in 2024. Participants were selected using systematic random sampling. Data were collected using checklists and structured interviewer‑administered questionnaires, entered into Epi‑Data 4.6.0, and analyzed with Stata 15. Time to first ANC contact was estimated using Kaplan–Meier survival analysis with log‑rank tests. Predictors of antenatal care initiation were identified using Cox proportional hazards regression; model adequacy was assessed using Cox–Snell residuals. Results: The mean survival time to antenatal care initiation was 7.4 months (95% CI: 7.08, 7.76). Earlier initiation was independently associated with higher maternal education (AHR = 1.65; 95% CI: 1.21, 2.25), urban residence (AHR = 1.96; 95% CI: 1.07, 3.59), having received counseling on antenatal care (AHR = 3.17; 95% CI: 1.18, 8.54), and good knowledge of antenatal care (AHR = 1.64; 95% CI: 1.14, 2.36). Longer delays were observed among women from female‑headed households (AHR = 0.46; 95% CI: 0.26, 0.81) and those with no prior exposure to obstetric ultrasound scans (AHR = 0.12; 95% CI: 0.04, 0.32). Conclusion and recommendation: Pregnant women in this pastoralist setting initiate antenatal care substantially later than World Health Organization recommendations. Educational attainment, place of residence, counseling, and antenatal care‑related knowledge were predictors of earlier initiation, whereas female‑headed household status and lack of prior ultrasound exposure contributed to delays. Targeted strategies including strengthening community-based health education tailored to pastoralist livelihoods, improving access in remote areas, expanding counseling services, supporting female‑headed households, and promoting ultrasound use are urgently needed to improve timely antenatal care uptake.

title: Primary Central nervous system vasculitis mimicking Tuberculous Meningitis: A case report
abstract: Abstract Background Primary central nervous system vasculitis (PCNSV) is a rare disease characterized by inflammatory infiltration of blood vessels in the central nervous system (CNS). Owing to the lack of specificity in its clinical features and imaging examinations, it is highly prone to being missed or misdiagnosed. Case presentation A 58-year-old female from South China was admitted with headache in March 2025. Brain MRI suggested possible intracranial inflammation, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) examination revealed increased cell counts, decreased glucose and chloride levels, and elevated protein levels. CNS viral infection was considered, and empirical antiviral and anti-inflammatory effects with penciclovir and dexamethasone yielded no improvement. Then, diagnostic anti-tuberculosis (TB) treatment was given, there was no improvement in symptoms. Weeks later, the patient's condition worsened, with persistent headache accompanied by nausea, vomiting, cognitive dysfunction and memory decline. Even after intensified steroid therapy, the response was still poor. A subsequent craniotomy biopsy confirmed central nervous system vasculitis. Conclusion This case illustrates that PCNSV can present with symptoms such as headaches and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid indicators, which closely resemble CNS infections. For patients with poor response to empirical antibiotic therapy, early biopsy can help improve diagnostic accuracy and prognosis.

title: Comparison of Oblique Lateral Interbody Fusion Combined with Minimally Invasive Transforaminal Lumbar Interbody Fusion versus Posterior Lumbar Interbody Fusion for Long-Segment (L2-S1) Degenerative Lumbar Spinal Stenosis
abstract: Abstract Objective Oblique lateral interbody fusion (OLIF) is widely used to treat degenerative lumbar disorders but is generally unsuitable for the L5-S1 level. We therefore combined OLIF at L2-L5 with minimally invasive transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (MIS-TLIF) at L5-S1 (hereafter referred to as OMAT) to treat long-segment (L2-S1) degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis (LDLS). This study compared the clinical and radiographic outcomes of OMAT and posterior lumbar interbody fusion (PLIF), with particular emphasis on perioperative recovery, surgical characteristics, and spinal alignment. Methods From May 2020 to May 2023, 27 patients with LDLS underwent either OMAT (n = 12) or PLIF (n = 15) at the Affiliated Hospital of Nantong University or the Affiliated Haian Hospital of Nantong University. We evaluated intraoperative blood loss, transfusion requirements, operative time, complications, and preoperative and postoperative Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) and visual analog scale (VAS) scores. Radiographic parameters, including anterior disc height (ADH), posterior disc height (PDH), lumbar lordosis (LL), and fused-segment lordosis (FSL), were also measured and compared between groups. Results No significant between-group differences were observed in postoperative LL or Cobb angle, indicating comparable deformity-correction efficacy. ADH and PDH were restored to a significantly greater extent in the OMAT group than in the PLIF group (P < 0.05). VAS and ODI scores improved significantly after surgery in both groups, with no significant between-group difference in postoperative improvement (P > 0.05). Conclusion Both OMAT and PLIF produced significant clinical improvement and satisfactory radiographic outcomes in patients with long-segment (L2-S1) degenerative lumbar disease. OMAT provided greater restoration of intervertebral height while achieving comparable correction of lumbar alignment and symptoms. Its less invasive approach may reduce tissue injury and facilitate postoperative recovery. Larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are required to confirm these findings.

title: A Prediction-Coupled Self-Explaining Functional Connectivity Learning Framework for rs-fMRI-Based Brain Disorder Classification
abstract: Abstract Existing resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) functional connectivity (FC) models can achieve useful predictive performance, but their explanations are often generated after prediction and are not systematically evaluated for faithfulness and reproducibility. We propose SE-FC, a prediction-coupled self-explaining functional connectivity framework for interpretable FC learning. The explanation pathway learns signed coefficients over FC edges, whose interaction with standardized FC values produces signed edge evidence that directly contributes to the final prediction. Deletion, insertion, and average output probability change (AOPC) analyses showed that SE-FC-derived evidence was more strongly associated with model output than random edge rankings. Cross-run analysis further quantified explanation reproducibility by identifying recurrent consensus patterns while characterizing substantial variability in exact edge selection across independent training runs. Predictive capability was evaluated as supporting evidence under strict leave-one-site-out validation on ABIDE (435 participants, 10 sites) and SRPBS (925 participants, six sites), with three independent repeated training runs for each dataset. SE-FC achieved AUC values of 0.6133 ± 0.0044 on ABIDE and 0.6127 ± 0.0051 on SRPBS, indicating competitive cross-site predictive capability. Overall, SE-FC provides prediction-coupled connectivity evidence with quantitatively assessed model-level faithfulness and cross-run reproducibility while retaining useful predictive performance.

title: Open-Set Recognition for Dental Implant System Identification: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Background Deep learning models for dental implant identification are typically trained on a fixed set of systems, although new systems continuously enter the market. Such closed-set models assign unregistered implants to known systems, often with high confidence. We compared open-set recognition methods for detecting unregistered implant systems while identifying registered ones. Methods In this retrospective study, 100,105 implant images from panoramic radiographs across 15 institutions were obtained from a public dataset. Thirteen systems with > 2,000 images were defined as known classes, while 29 systems (14,004 images) were withheld as unknown classes. A ConvNeXt classifier was trained using ten implant-level splits. Score-based, distance-based (OpenMax), and training-based (ARPL) methods were compared at a threshold accepting 95% of known validation images. Results The classifier achieved 0.901 accuracy for system identification and 0.968 accuracy at the manufacturer level. OpenMax achieved an AUROC of 0.898 and detected 61.4% of unknown images with 0.868 precision, outperforming all other methods across ten splits (AUROC, 0.825–0.844; detection, 29.1–49.4%; adjusted P = 0.012). Its advantage was retained after excluding institutions without known-class images. Unknown systems from manufacturers represented in training were harder to detect than those from new manufacturers (57.5% vs. 64.4%), and undetected implants were often assigned to a small number of known systems, frequently from the same manufacturer. Conclusions Closed-set evaluation overlooks a major risk of automated implant identification. A post hoc distance-based method detected most unregistered implants without retraining and with minimal loss of closed-set accuracy, providing a practical safeguard for existing classifiers and supporting expert review of flagged cases.

title: Diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease Based on Multimodal MRI and Amyloid/Tau PET Fusion: Quantification of Modality Complementarity and Interpretability Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis relies on multimodal information, yet the optimal fusion strategy and the true complementarity among modalities remain unclear. This study aimed to systematically compare different modality configurations for AD diagnosis and to quantify modality complementarity. Methods: A total of 874 participants from the ADNI cohort (CN = 608, AD = 266) were included. A total of 39 features were extracted, comprising structural MRI (20 features), amyloid PET (5), Tau PET (10), and clinical variables (4). We employed a three-step feature selection process using variance thresholding, t-tests, and LASSO to evaluate 7 modality configurations and 5 classifiers, and quantified modality complementarity using centered kernel alignment (CKA), Pearson correlation coefficients, and the Jaccard index. Results: The multimodal fusion model achieved an AUC of 0.9558 in the full dataset and 0.9910 in the complete PET subset, outperforming all single-modality and dual-modality combinations. The Jaccard index for MRI and PET was 0.0000, indicating no overlap in misclassification patterns. SHAP analysis indicated that the hippocampal volume ratio (HIPPO_RATIO) was the most important feature. Conclusions: Multimodal fusion integrating structural MRI, amyloid/Tau PET, and clinical variables provides a robust and interpretable tool for AD diagnosis. More importantly, it addresses a key technical gap in multimodal research---the lack of a quantitative framework for assessing modality complementarity---by demonstrating that MRI and PET exhibit completely non-overlapping error patterns, which constitutes the core mechanism driving the improved performance of multimodal fusion.

title: VarSee™ (Lung), a Blood-Based Multi-Protein Biomarker Panel for the Early Detection of Lung Cancer: A Prospective Pilot Diagnostic Accuracy Study
abstract: Abstract Background Most non-small-cell lung cancers are diagnosed at an advanced stage because early disease is largely asymptomatic. Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT), the recommended screening modality for high-risk individuals, is constrained by radiation exposure, limited accessibility and a high false-positive rate. We evaluated VarSee™(Lung), a serum multi-protein biomarker panel coupled to a machine-learning classifier, as a blood-based adjunct for lung-cancer detection. Methods In a consecutive, prospective, single-centre, case-control pilot study with biomarker measurement performed retrospectively on banked serum samples, seven serum proteins (CA125, CA19-9, carcinoembryonic antigen [CEA], cytokeratin-19 fragment [CYFRA 21 − 1], human epididymis protein 4 [HE4], neuron-specific enolase [NSE] and progastrin-releasing peptide [ProGRP]), quantified by chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA), together with the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and four clinical covariates, were measured in 100 participants (50 with histologically confirmed lung cancer and 50 non-cancer controls) and entered into a calibrated random-forest classifier (the VarSee™ (Lung) algorithm) to generate a diagnostic score. Diagnostic performance was assessed against a histopathological/CT reference standard using stratified five-fold cross-validation, reported in accordance with STARD 2015 and, for the multivariable model, TRIPOD. Results VarSee™ (Lung) distinguished lung-cancer cases from controls with a sensitivity of 100% (95% CI 92.9–100), a specificity of 96.0% (95% CI 86.5–98.9), a positive predictive value of 96.2%, a negative predictive value of 100%, an accuracy of 98.0% (95% CI 93.0-99.4) and an area under the ROC curve of 0.997 ((95% CI 0.990–1.000). In this small cohort, sensitivity was 100% at every tumour stage (I-IV). The NLR was the dominant predictor (impurity importance 0.501), followed by CA19-9 (0.116) and CYFRA 21 − 1 (0.066); accuracy and AUC were consistent across five candidate classification algorithms (accuracy 0.950–0.980; AUC 0.995–0.997). Conclusions In this pilot, a blood-based seven-protein panel integrated with the NLR discriminated lung cancer from cancer-free controls with high sensitivity and specificity, supporting further evaluation as a radiation-free adjunct for early detection. Given the small, single-centre design and cancer-free (rather than benign-disease-matched) controls, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in a larger, multi-centre study with external validation before any clinical or screening application is considered. Trial registration: Clinical Trials Registry - India, CTRI/2026/03/105171. Retrospectively registered (enrolment began prior to registration).

title: Prevalence and Factors Associated With Incidental Prostate Cancer After Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Surgery: A Five-Year Retrospective Study in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Background Incidental prostate cancer (IPC), defined as cancer unexpectedly identified on histopathology after surgery for presumed benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), has been widely studied internationally, but data from sub-Saharan Africa remain scarce, and none exist from Ethiopia. This study examined the prevalence, predictors, clinicopathological features, and management of IPC among patients undergoing transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) or transvesical prostatectomy (TVP) for presumed BPH. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 239 patients who underwent TURP or TVP for presumed BPH at MCM Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, between January 2021 and December 2025. Sociodemographic, clinical, laboratory, and procedural data were abstracted from medical records. Bivariable comparisons used chi-square or Fisher's exact tests and t-tests or Mann–Whitney U tests, as appropriate; univariable and multivariable logistic regression estimated crude and adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Model fit and discrimination were assessed, and sensitivity analyses examined robustness to prostate-specific antigen (PSA) transformation and influential observations Results IPC was identified in 23 of 239 patients (9.6%), with no significant difference by procedure (TURP 11.1% vs. TVP 8.2%, p = 0.445). Patients with IPC had significantly higher rates of hypertension (47.8% vs. 26.4%, p = 0.030), hydronephrosis (39.1% vs. 14.4%, p = 0.006), acute kidney injury (39.1% vs. 8.3%, p < 0.001), and higher PSA and PSA density (both p < 0.001). On multivariable analysis, preoperative PSA (AOR = 1.25 per ng/mL, 95% CI: 1.14–1.38), diabetes mellitus (AOR = 5.28, 95% CI: 1.64–16.95), and hydronephrosis (AOR = 3.92, 95% CI: 1.29–11.94) were independently associated with IPC; age was not (AOR = 1.19 per decade, p = 0.459). The model showed good discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.838) and calibration (Hosmer–Lemeshow p = 0.162), with findings robust across sensitivity analyses. Among IPC cases, 95.7% had International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) Grade Group ≥ 2, yet no patient received active surveillance, radical prostatectomy, radiotherapy, or documented staging investigation; management was uniformly based on androgen deprivation. Conclusions IPC affected nearly 1 in 10 men undergoing BPH surgery, with PSA, diabetes mellitus, and hydronephrosis independently associated with it; PSA density > 0.15 had 90% specificity but only 48% sensitivity. Most cases were clinically significant, yet none received staging or definitive local therapy, highlighting the need for structured incidental-cancer care pathways in similar resource-limited settings.

title: Photoacoustic imaging of human brain function through intact adult skulls
abstract: Abstract Blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) has revolutionized noninvasive imaging of human brain function, but it indirectly senses deoxyhemoglobin through water-proton relaxation and relies on bulky, costly, noisy, enclosed, superconducting-magnet scanners. In contrast, photoacoustic computed tomography (PACT) directly probes hemoglobin absorption using a more compact, lower-cost, quieter, open, magnet-free system. However, functional PACT of the adult human brain has so far been demonstrated only after surgical skull removal, because the skull strongly attenuates optical and acoustic signals. Here, we demonstrate non-invasive transcranial functional PACT (T-fPACT) through the intact adult skull. A densely packed, high-channel-count (3,072-element) hemispherical ultrasonic array provides near-2π-steradian simultaneous acquisition, enabling high sensitivity and single-shot three-dimensional imaging at 20 Hz that eliminates motion blurring. Participant-specific stabilization further enables measurement of small task-evoked hemodynamic responses over the entire task duration. In healthy adults, T-fPACT localized responses to expected sensorimotor regions, distinguished task-specific motor representations, and yielded consistent localizations across repeated task runs and visits. Comparison with high-field (7 T) fMRI showed spatially corresponding functional regions, while dual-wavelength imaging revealed distinct hemoglobin-weighted responses. These findings overcome the long-standing skull barrier in human brain PACT and establish non-invasive, rapid volumetric photoacoustic imaging of brain function.

title: Three-dimensional morphometry of the normal nasal septum on computed tomography: sex- and age-specific reference values from 1,373 adults
abstract: Abstract Purpose. Normative data for the three-dimensional anatomy of the nasal septum are sparse. We applied automated segmentation to a large series of adults with radiologically normal sinonasal anatomy to establish sex- and age-specific reference values for septal size, thickness, and midline deviation. Methods. Retrospective cross-sectional study of 1,373 adults (394 men, 979 women; age 18 to 90 years) with sinus computed tomography reported as normal. The septum was segmented by a validated three-dimensional convolutional network (held-out Dice 0.983), and 12 parameters were computed from each segmentation: volume, surface area, maximal and mean sagittal cross-sectional area, three linear extents, three thickness measures, and maximal midline deviation and deviation angle. Reference percentiles were computed by sex and by sex within four age bands; age trends were estimated by linear and quantile regression. Results. Median septal volume was 16,710 mm³ in men (5th to 95th percentile 13,594 to 20,455) and 12,500 mm³ in women (9,963 to 15,329); median mean thickness was 4.89 and 4.29 mm. All size and thickness parameters were larger in men. In men, volume, depth, height, and maximal thickness increased by 1.2 to 1.4% per decade of age; in women they were constant (sex-by-age interaction P ≤ 0.021). Midline deviation did not vary with age, and its 95th percentile was about 3 mm in both sexes. Conclusion. These sex- and age-specific percentiles provide a quantitative reference for interpreting septal anatomy on computed tomography, planning septal surgery, and selecting reference geometries for airflow modeling.

title: Predicting recurrence of biliary colic after conservative management in the emergency department: a prospective cohort study with a parametric Weibull survival model
abstract: Abstract Background Biliary colic is usually managed conservatively in the emergency department (ED), yet recurrence is frequent and its timing is poorly characterized, particularly in Latin American settings with limited access to elective cholecystectomy. We aimed to develop and internally validate a survival-based model predicting recurrence of biliary colic after conservative ED management. Methods Single-center prospective cohort of adults with uncomplicated biliary colic and ultrasound-confirmed gallstones discharged from the ED of a tertiary hospital in Cuenca, Ecuador, followed for up to 365 days. The primary outcome was symptomatic recurrence requiring an ED visit; cholecystectomy and biliary complications before recurrence were censored. Predictors were screened with Cox regression; multivariable Cox and parametric Weibull models were compared by Harrell's C-index and the Akaike information criterion. Internal validation used 1000 bootstrap resamples; calibration was assessed at 7, 15, 30 and 60 days overall and by predicted-risk group. A sensitivity analysis used Fine–Gray competing-risks regression. Results Of 507 patients (median age 38 years; 76.5% women), 223 (44.0%) recurred; 25% of recurrences occurred within 7 days of discharge and recurrence-free survival was 67.8% at 30 days and 43.1% at 365 days. Biliary complications developed in 10.7% and only 7.3% underwent cholecystectomy before recurrence. In the final Weibull model, a positive Murphy's sign (hazard ratio [HR] 7.09; 95% CI 4.73–10.61) and diabetes mellitus (HR 2.18; 95% CI 1.33–3.58) were independent predictors. The shape parameter (γ = 0.419; 95% CI 0.376–0.468) indicated a monotonically decreasing baseline hazard. Discrimination was acceptable (C-index 0.692; bootstrap-corrected 0.692, 95% CI 0.665–0.723) with good calibration from 30 days onwards and underestimation of very early risk in the highest-risk group. Fine–Gray estimates were consistent (subdistribution HR 5.73 and 2.06, respectively). Conclusions Recurrence after conservative management of biliary colic is frequent and concentrated in the first days after discharge. Two bedside variables, Murphy's sign and diabetes mellitus, identify patients at high risk of early recurrence who may benefit from prioritized surgical evaluation and structured early follow-up. External validation in multicenter cohorts is required. Trial registration: Not applicable (observational study).

title: A Lesion-Guided Deep Learning Framework for Differential Diagnosis of Pulmonary Nodules: A Pathology-Confirmed Study of Pulmonary Tuberculosis, Lung Cancer, Pulmonary Cryptococcosis, and Other Granulomatous Lung Lesions
abstract: Abstract Background Pulmonary tuberculous nodules frequently exhibit imaging features that overlap with those of lung cancer, pulmonary cryptococcosis, and other granulomatous lesions, making accurate preoperative diagnosis challenging and often resulting in unnecessary surgical intervention. We developed a lesion-guided deep learning framework to improve the differential diagnosis of surgically resected pulmonary nodules on chest CT. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 1,084 patients with surgically confirmed pulmonary nodules, comprising pulmonary tuberculosis (n = 240), pulmonary cryptococcosis (n = 298), other granulomatous inflammatory lesions (n = 252), and lung malignancies (n = 294). We developed a lesion-guided dual-branch UNet (LG-DU-Net) that jointly performed lesion segmentation and classification in an end-to-end framework. Model performance was compared with five representative deep learning models using multiple binary and multi-class classification tasks. Results LG-DU-Net consistently achieved the best diagnostic performance across all classification tasks. In benign–malignant classification, the model achieved an AUC of 0.880. The highest performance was observed in differentiating pulmonary tuberculosis from pulmonary cryptococcosis, with an AUC of 0.972 and an accuracy of 89.8%. In the three-class classification task involving pulmonary tuberculosis, pulmonary cryptococcosis, and other granulomatous inflammatory lesions, the model achieved a macro-average AUC of 0.862. Grad-CAM visualization demonstrated that model predictions were primarily driven by lesion-related imaging features. Conclusion LG-DU-Net enables accurate and interpretable differentiation of pulmonary tuberculosis, lung cancer, pulmonary cryptococcosis, and other granulomatous pulmonary nodules using chest CT images. The proposed framework has the potential to improve preoperative diagnostic accuracy, facilitate appropriate clinical management, and reduce unnecessary surgical intervention.

title: Radiographic Measurement of Psoas Muscle Width as a Predictor of Cage Subsidence Following Transforaminal Lumbar Interbody Fusion
abstract: Abstract Objective Cage subsidence is a common complication after transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF). We evaluated whether preoperative radiographic psoas muscle width (PMW), measured on routine lumbar radiographs, is independently associated with cage subsidence after single-level TLIF. Methods This retrospective single-center study included 262 patients undergoing single-level TLIF between 2018 and 2023. PMW was measured at the L3 inferior endplate on preoperative standing anteroposterior radiographs. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the independent association between PMW and subsidence; a PMW-by-sex interaction term was tested and sex-stratified receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed, with bootstrap internal validation. Results Cage subsidence occurred in 58 patients (22.14%). Patients with subsidence had significantly lower PMW (98.33 ± 9.24 mm vs. 112.72 ± 10.42 mm, p < 0.001) and volumetric bone mineral density (105.36 ± 19.98 mg/cm³ vs. 134.34 ± 29.80 mg/cm³, p < 0.001). In the multivariable model, PMW remained an independent predictor (OR 0.815, 95% CI 0.765, 0.869; p < 0.001), as did sex and vBMD. Sex-stratified ROC analysis demonstrated good discriminatory performance: AUC 0.870 for males (cutoff 112.25 mm; sensitivity 0.842, specificity 0.798) and AUC 0.886 for females (cutoff 101.05 mm; sensitivity 0.846, specificity 0.820). Interobserver reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.914). Conclusion Lower preoperative radiographic PMW was independently associated with cage subsidence after single-level TLIF. PMW may help identify patients at low risk, but the sex-specific cutoff values are exploratory and require external validation.

title: Sex estimation from the three-dimensional nasal septum on computed tomography: an allometric, size-based signal in 1,373 adults
abstract: Abstract Sex estimation from computed tomography (CT) of the head has relied on manual measurements of the skull, paranasal sinuses, and nasal cavity, with modest accuracy and small samples. The nasal septum, the midline osteocartilaginous partition of the nasal cavity, is present on every head CT but has never been evaluated as a sex estimator, and whether any sex signal in the septum reflects size or shape determines how such an estimator would transfer between populations. We tested two hypotheses in 1,373 adults (394 men, 979 women) with radiologically normal sinus CT: that septal morphometry classifies sex at least as accurately as established cranial methods, and that the discriminating information is allometric size rather than shape. The septum was segmented automatically with a validated convolutional network (held-out Dice 0.983) and 17 morphometric variables were derived from each segmentation. Septal volume was 34% larger in men (16,852 versus 12,564 mm³; Cohen's d 2.33, 95% CI 2.18 to 2.47). Under five-fold cross-validation, sex was classified with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.95 by random forest and 0.96 by logistic regression on 17 variables; volume alone gave 0.94. After allometric adjustment no shape variable differed by more than d = 0.43, and shape variables alone gave an AUC of 0.58 to 0.63. Both hypotheses were supported: the septum is a strong, fully automatable sex estimator for CT, and its signal is size. Like other size-based skeletal estimators it will require population-specific calibration, which the automated pipeline makes practical.

title: Femoral medullary composition in advanced post mortem decomposition: agreement of attenuation-based volumetric fractions across two PMCT reconstruction protocols
abstract: Abstract In advanced decomposition, conventional post mortem markers become progressively less informative, whereas bone and medullary content remain comparatively preserved. This retrospective study assessed whether femoral medullary composition can be quantified consistently on post mortem computed tomography (PMCT) using a semi-automated segmentation approach and whether attenuation-based volumetric fractions are associated with cadaveric alteration. PMCT examinations from 100 decomposed forensic cases (199 femora) were analysed with the SegMed module in 3D Slicer. Eight medullary fractions were quantified using soft-tissue (ST) and bone (BN) reconstruction protocols. Agreement was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), paired Wilcoxon tests and Bland–Altman analysis; associations with the Radiological Alteration Index (RAI) and estimated post mortem interval (PMI) were assessed using Spearman correlations with Benjamini–Hochberg correction. Agreement between ST and BN reconstructions was excellent for gas, fat-like marrow, fluid and intermediate-density fractions (ICCs > 0.94), despite small systematic offsets, whereas agreement was lower for residual medullary content on the right (ICC = 0.52) and unstable for debris. Gas fractions were positively associated with RAI, whereas fluid and intermediate-density fractions were negatively associated (|ρ| approximately 0.25–0.37). No volumetric fraction was significantly associated with estimated PMI after correction. Semi-automated PMCT segmentation therefore yielded consistent measurements of the principal femoral medullary fractions across the two reconstruction protocols evaluated. These fractions are candidate quantitative markers of radiological cadaveric alteration, but their value for elapsed-time estimation requires validation in cohorts with more accurately known PMIs.

title: Primary Cardiac Synovial Sarcoma of the Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Mimicking Cardiac Myxoma
abstract: Abstract Background: Primary cardiac synovial sarcoma (PCSS) is exceedingly rare and typically presents with imaging features characteristic of malignancy, including aggressive growth, poorly defined margins, and limited mobility. However, a subset of cases may closely mimic a myxoma with a benign imaging phenotype, thereby posing a significant preoperative diagnostic pitfall and compromising treatment planning. Case summary: A 34-year-old man was admitted with acute cerebral infarction. Echocardiography and coronary CTA demonstrated a solid, pedunculated subaortic mass attached to the left ventricular outflow tract, with marked mobility and imaging features highly consistent with a myxoma. Given the acute phase of cerebral infarction and high perioperative risk, tumor resection was deferred following multidisciplinary team discussion. At 4-month follow-up, the mass showed a mild interval increase in size, and open-heart surgery with mass excision was performed. Intraoperatively, the tumor exhibited a botryoid, semi-translucent appearance but was soft externally and firm internally on palpation. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry revealed positivity for TLE1 and SS18-SSX, and FISH confirmed SS18 gene rearrangement, establishing the diagnosis of PCSS. Adjuvant chemotherapy was administered postoperatively, with no evidence of residual tumor on follow-up imaging. Discussion: This case highlights that PCSS may completely mimic the growth pattern of a myxoma in its early phase, including a pedunculated attachment, marked mobility, and well-circumscribed borders—imaging features that readily lead to a benign misdiagnosis. For masses located in atypical locations with benign imaging features but complicated by systemic embolization, a high index of suspicion for malignancy should be maintained.

title: Routine perioperative radiographs for early risk stratification of femoral head osteonecrosis after femoral neck fracture fixation: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Femoral head osteonecrosis (ONFH) after internal fixation of femoral neck fracture is difficult to predict before definitive radiographic changes appear. Preoperative and immediate postoperative radiographs may contain prognostic information not fully captured by routine patient characteristics and visual radiographic grades. We compared a four-view radiographic model with a six-variable conventional baseline and explored the value of combining clinical and imaging information. Methods This single-centre retrospective cohort included 877 adults treated with closed reduction and cannulated compression screw fixation (CCS), of whom 222 developed ONFH. The development set comprised 727 patients, and 150 formed a fixed internal test set. The conventional baseline was a logistic regression model using age, sex, body mass index, time from admission to surgery, fracture displacement and reduction quality. The four-view model used preoperative and immediate postoperative anteroposterior and lateral radiographs. The primary measure was the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC); the area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC), Brier score and calibration were also assessed. Uncertainty and paired differences were estimated by patient-level bootstrap resampling; the preoperative–postoperative biplanar comparison used DeLong's test. Results In the test set, the four-view model had an AUROC of 0.864 versus 0.704 for the conventional baseline, a paired difference of 0.160 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.068–0.256). The corresponding AUPRCs were 0.759 and 0.432, a paired difference of 0.327 (95% CI 0.153–0.461). Brier scores were 0.148 and 0.171, respectively. The uncalibrated four-view probabilities showed calibration error. An exploratory model combining the six variables with the four-view output had an AUROC of 0.863 and showed no additional discrimination. Conclusions A model using four routine radiographic views obtained before and immediately after fixation discriminated subsequent ONFH better than the six-variable conventional baseline, whereas fusion did not improve discrimination. External validation and calibration assessment are needed before using predicted probabilities to guide individual follow-up decisions. title: Technical Note: SegMed, a 3D Slicer module for standardized post mortem CT segmentation of lower-limb long-bone diaphyses
abstract: Abstract Post mortem computed tomography is increasingly used in forensic medicine and anthropology, but quantitative analysis of skeletal and peri-skeletal structures remains limited by heterogeneous anatomical sampling and manual segmentation procedures. This Technical Note presents SegMed, a Python-based 3D Slicer module developed to standardize segmentation and metric extraction from lower-limb long-bone post mortem CT data. In its current version, SegMed is restricted to the lower limb, and the present manuscript focuses on femoral and tibial diaphyseal workflows. The module integrates four steps: semi-automatic extraction of the diaphyseal region from an expert-defined cortical seed point, anatomical alignment of the selected bone segment, Hounsfield unit (HU)-based segmentation of medullary compartments, and optional quantification of peridiaphyseal soft tissues. The module exports quality-control masks, compartment volumes, volumetric fractions, longitudinal profiles, metadata files and analysis-ready CSV/XLSX tables. Optional exploratory indices describing the spatial distribution of segmented compartments are exported for research purposes but are not evaluated in this Technical Note. By combining expert-guided initialization with standardized image processing and structured outputs, SegMed is intended to improve reproducibility in forensic imaging research. The software does not provide diagnostic conclusions, and all outputs require expert visual review and contextual interpretation.

title: AI-based MRI brain parcellation reveals region-specific structural remodeling after glioma resection: a longitudinal paired-imaging cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Quantitative postoperative glioma MRI remains predominantly lesion-centered, while structural remodeling of non-tumor brain and cerebrospinal-fluid compartments is incompletely characterized. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 64 adults with morphologically verified gliomas and technically adequate paired preoperative and postoperative 3D T1-weighted MRI. An automated neural-network Brain Parcellation workflow segmented approximately 110 anatomical regions. Ventricular and CSF volumes were evaluated in the full paired cohort. Whole-brain lobar volumes and interhemispheric asymmetry were additionally assessed in a 30-patient paired subset and compared with 30 demographically comparable healthy controls. Paired tests were selected according to distribution, Hedges' g summarized between-group effects, Spearman correlation assessed associations with tumor diameter, and false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction addressed multiplicity. Results: Right lateral ventricular volume increased from a median 5.11 to 6.29 mL (P = 0.03), third ventricular volume from 0.80 to 0.87 mL (P = 0.03), and fourth ventricular volume from 1.80 to 2.00 mL (P < 0.05), while total CSF volume remained stable (P = 0.38). Postoperative patients had lower parietal (-10.7%; g = 0.53; q = 0.002), occipital (-11.2%; g = 0.50; q = 0.002), and frontal (-8.4%; g = 0.41; q = 0.011) volumes than controls. Temporal volume was not significantly different (-3.8%; q = 0.35), but temporal asymmetry differed strongly (mean asymmetry index 0.092 vs -0.003; g=-0.55; q = 0.001). Tumor diameter showed no FDR-significant association with lobar, asymmetry, or ventricular measures. Conclusions: Automated MRI parcellation identified heterogeneous postoperative remodeling characterized by selective ventricular change, region-specific lobar differences, and persistent temporal asymmetry. Whole-brain quantitative morphometry may complement residual-tumor assessment, although external validation is required.

title: SRD U-Net: Spatial Refined Depthwise U-Net forRetinal Vessel Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Precise pixel level categorization of retinal vessels requires both deep contextualawareness and distortion free spatial representation. Traditional encoder-decodermodels often suffer from excessive parameter counts and an inability to prioritizesignificant feature spaces selectively. Consequently sub optimal boundaries andnoise propagation are presents in the retinal vascular fundus images. To addressthese limitations, this paper introduces the contrast-aware retinal preprocessorblock(CARP) and spatial refined depthwise U-Net (SRD U-Net). The CARPserves as a retinal image preprocess and augmentation module that enhancescontrast and sharpness. The CARP uses contrast-limited adaptive histogramequalization and TensorFlow-based luma?chroma sharpening to generate preprocesseddatasets for segmentation tasks. The SRD U-Net is a lightweight highlydiscriminative segmentation network with three blocks including conventionalfilter depthwise unit (CFDU) encoder, channel attention bottleneck(CAB) andCFDU decoder. . The core of our proposed architecture lies in a novel hybridfeature-extraction sequence, CFDU. The CFDU block initially captures primitivespatial patterns through a standard 2D convolution. The convolution outputtransitioning to a manual depthwise separable configuration, decoupling spatialfiltering from channel mixing to dramatically compress the network parameter.Furthermore, we combat feature redundancy in the latent space by integratinga channel attention bottleneck(CAB). The CAB block aggregates global contextthrough spatial pooling to dynamically compute non-linear inter channel dependencies.The bottleneck attention mechanism explicitly recalibrates channel-wiseresponses with highly informative feature maps. In addition, the bottlenecksystematically suppresses attention, filtering out irrelevant background noise.Furthermore, we evaluated our framework with DRIVE, HRF, STARE, CHASEand FIVES datasets. The performance metrics used for assessment of proposedframework are accuracy, sensitivity, F1 score, recall and precision. On averageacross all datasets, our proposed method afforded improvements of approximately2 % among all metrics compared to the lowest-performing baseline. Finally,our model achieves comparable accuracy with significantly lower computationaloverhead, featuring reduced parameter size and faster execution speeds. Thisportrays our approach as a highly efficient alternative for resource-constrainedenvironments.

title: Non-invasive Detection of Neuronal Electrical Activity in the Knee Joint Using Quantum Sensing MRI
abstract: Abstract Noninvasive assessment of neuronal activity in the knee may improve understanding of osteoarthritis (OA)-related pain and joint degeneration. A 3T quantum-sensing based MRI framework was developed to estimate firing-rate-related signal fluctuations from free induction decay (FID) phase measurements, separating water and fat signals for compartment-specific estimates. The approach was evaluated in agar-gel phantoms, simulations, and six healthy volunteers and six participants with early knee OA, at rest and during repeated ankle flexion. No firing events were detected in the phantom. Simulation performance improved with signal-to-noise ratio, reaching R 2 = 0.99 at SNR = 250. In vivo, water-derived estimates correlated negatively with T 1ρ relaxation times (cartilage, r = -0.86 to -0.58; meniscus, r = -0.78 to -0.73). Fat-derived estimates differentiated OA participants from healthy volunteers (d = 3.96–4.89; p < 0.05), correlated positively with T 1ρ (cartilage r = 0.59–0.70; meniscus r = 0.70–0.71) and showed moderate exploratory associations with WOMAC scores (r = 0.43–0.55). Repeatability was higher during ankle flexion than at rest. These findings support the technical feasibility of compartment-specific FID phase analysis in the knee. Larger studies with physiological-noise control and independent biological validation are required to determine whether these MRI-derived measures specifically reflect peripheral neuronal activity and have clinical utility in OA.

title: Classification of Lung Cancer Subtypes In Thoracic CT-Scan Images Using Gray Level Run Length Matrix (GLRLM) and Support Vector Machine (SVM)
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate classification of lung cancer subtypes remains a critical challenge in medical imaging because of inter-observer variability and the need for interpretable diagnostic systems. Deep learning achieves high accuracy, but its black-box nature limits clinical interpretability and trust. Materials and Methods This quantitative descriptive study evaluated an interpretable classification system that combines Gray Level Run Length Matrix (GLRLM) texture features with a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier. The study analyzed 260 thorax computed tomography (CT) images from The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA), comprising four equal classes: normal, adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and large cell carcinoma. Preprocessing included 36×36 pixel region of interest (ROI) cropping and grayscale normalization, and seven GLRLM features were extracted from four orientations. A one-vs-all multi-class SVM was trained on 200 images and tested on 60 hold-out images, with 5-fold cross-validation. Results The system achieved 100% performance on the hold-out test set, which should be interpreted cautiously given the small and controlled dataset. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an average accuracy of 98.5 ± 1.4%. Normal lungs showed a rough texture with heterogeneous gray-level distribution, adenocarcinoma a rough texture with homogeneous distribution, squamous cell carcinoma a smooth texture with homogeneous distribution, and large cell carcinoma a smooth texture with heterogeneous distribution. Conclusion The GLRLM-SVM approach provides accurate and interpretable classification of lung cancer subtypes, with textural features that correspond to known pathological characteristics. It may support clinical decision-making where model explanations are critical.

title: Qualitative CT Features as Predictors of Microscopic Perinephric Fat Invasion in Renal Cell Carcinoma: Towards a Radiomics-Informed Staging Framework
abstract: Abstract Purpose Up to 14% of cT1 renal cell carcinomas (RCC) treated with partial nephrectomy are upstaged to pT3a owing to microscopic perinephric fat invasion (PFI) not visible on preoperative computed tomography (CT). We aimed to identify reproducible qualitative CT predictors of microscopic PFI. Methods Consecutive patients undergoing partial nephrectomy for cT1 RCC without overt local invasion (2009–2020) were enrolled in a prospective database. Pre-specified CT features were scored by a blinded primary radiologist and re-scored by two further blinded readers. Associations with PFI were modelled using Firth penalised logistic regression and inter-reader agreement with Fleiss’ κ. A two-feature nomogram was internally validated by bootstrap. Results Of 135 patients, 117 formed the imaging cohort; 10 (8.5%) had PFI. Tumour margin irregularity (odds ratio [OR] 5.20, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.45–22.6) and perinephric neovascularity (OR 4.84, 95% CI 1.31–18.0) predicted PFI on univariable analysis, whereas fat stranding did not (OR 0.95). Three-reader agreement was substantial (κ 0.67–0.74). After mutual adjustment, neither feature remained significant (margin irregularity OR 3.56, 95% CI 0.78–17.8; neovascularity OR 2.41, 95% CI 0.55–10.9). The nomogram achieved an optimism-corrected area under the curve of 0.71 (apparent 0.73, 95% CI 0.54–0.90). Conclusion Margin irregularity and neovascularity are candidate CT predictors of microscopic PFI in cT1 RCC, whereas peritumoural fat stranding is not. Tumour margin irregularity, the strongest univariable predictor with substantial inter-reader agreement, is a practical marker to report when staging cT1 RCC and a biologically anchored target for future radiomics models, pending external validation.

title: Transcranial optical and optoacoustic super-resolution cortical microangiography in aged and Alzheimer mice
abstract: Abstract Cerebrovascular alterations and dysfunction are increasingly recognized as key contributors to aging and Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet longitudinal in vivo imaging of cortical microvascular networks remains challenged by limited penetration of ballistic photons and transcranial ultrasound aberrations. While super-resolution ultrasound (SRUS) has enabled unprecedented capabilities for microangiography via microbubble localization and tracking, aberrations arising from bidirectional ultrasound propagation through the thickened skull of aged mice remain a significant challenge, often necessitating cranial windows. Here, we propose a complementary localization-based framework combining diffuse optical localization imaging (DOLI) and localization optoacoustic tomography (LOT) for super-resolution vascular imaging in aged and AD mice. DOLI capitalizes on the reduced light scattering in the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) to achieve transcranial visualization of the cortical microvasculature, while LOT leverages the unidirectional ultrasound propagation in optoacoustics to resolve pial microvessels and penetrating branches in a fully non-invasive manner. Both modalities reveal structural microvascular alterations in aging and AD, including increased vessel convolution and tortuosity at different scales, highlighting their potential for longitudinal studies of cerebrovascular pathology.

title: T2WI-based intratumoral habitat and peritumoral radiomics to predict lymph node metastasis in cervical cancer: a multicenter study with biological validation
abstract: Abstract Background To develop and validate a T2WI-based nomogram integrating intratumoral habitat imaging, peritumoral radiomics, and clinical features for preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in cervical cancer (CC), and to verify the biological plausibility of imaging habitats using an animal model. Methods This multicenter study included 766 CC patients (IB1-IIA2 and IIIC) from four centers, divided into training (n = 219), internal validation (n = 94), and two external test cohorts (n = 269, n = 184) between 2020 and 2024. Habitat imaging and peritumoral features were extracted, followed by machine‑learning model construction, evaluation, and SHAP interpretability. For biological validation, 12 nude mice bearing HeLa, SiHa, and U14 tumors underwent 9.4T MRI; imaging-pathology spatial registration was performed using 3D-printed molds, and habitat consistency was quantified by the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) and intraclass correlation coefficient for area (ICC(area)). Results Clinical stage and tumor diameter ≥ 4 cm were independent risk factors for LNM (both P < 0.05). The combined model yielded AUCs of 0.933 (training), 0.898 (internal validation), and 0.858–0.863 (external tests). A nomogram with a Youden-derived cutoff of 0.32 demonstrated consistent sensitivity (0.818–0.913) and specificity (0.732–0.877) across cohorts, with good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.183–0.561). Animal experiments revealed moderate spatial correspondence (ARI: 0.4–0.6) and high proportional consistency (ICC (area): 0.8–1.0) between imaging and pathological habitats. Conclusions This T2WI-based intratumoral habitat and peritumoral radiomics model provides accurate, economical preoperative LNM prediction for CC to guide personalized radiotherapy or surgery, with biological validity confirmed by animal experiments. Trial registration ChiCTR2400081731, Registered 11 March 2024, https//www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=203940

title: Core Decompression via the Flip Cutter Technique Using an Expandable Reamer Augmented with Platelet-Rich Plasma and Calcium Phosphate Cement for Early-Stage (ARCO 1–2) Avascular Necrosis of the Femoral Head: A Single Centre Retrospective Observational Study
abstract: Abstract Background Avascular necrosis of the femoral head (AVNFH) frequently progresses to subchondral collapse and requires total hip arthroplasty if untreated. Core decompression (CD) provides a joint preserving intervention for early-stage disease. This study evaluates the short-term clinical and radiological outcomes of CD using the flip cutter technique of expandable reamer (ER), augmented with platelet-rich plasma (PRP) and calcium phosphate cement (CPC). Methods This uncontrolled retrospective single-centre observational study evaluated 25 hips in patients with symptomatic ARCO stage 1–2 AVNFH treated between January 2023 and January 2025. The surgical technique involved sequential debridement of necrotic bone through a minimal cortical window using ER, followed by PRP injection and sealing of the cortical defect with CPC. Patients were encouraged to bear weight immediately as tolerated. Outcomes were assessed in 6 weeks, and 3, 6, and 12 months using Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain scores, Harris Hip Scores (HHS), hip range of motion (ROM), and serial imaging, including a 1-year follow-up MRI. Results At the 12-month follow-up, the combined intervention was associated with a significant improvement in mean VAS pain scores, HHS and hip ROM (p < 0.05). Radiographic and MRI assessments confirmed no disease progression or subchondral collapse in any hip at one-year. The day-case procedure was performed safely with no recorded complications. Conclusion In this small retrospective study, ER-assisted core decompression with PRP and CPC was associated with improved short-term pain and functional scores, with no observed subchondral collapse or conversion to THA during approximately one year of follow-up. These findings should be interpreted as preliminary observations rather than evidence of definitive efficacy, and they require confirmation in adequately powered prospective comparative studies with longer-term follow-up. Novelty Statement By evaluating a tri-modal, minimally invasive technique combining expandable reamer debridement, platelet-rich plasma augmentation, and a calcium phosphate cement seal, this study provides preliminary evidence that this combined approach can potentially arrest disease progression and prevent subchondral collapse at one-year follow-up. Trial Registration: Not applicable, as this evaluation is based on retrospective clinical data and does not constitute a prospective healthcare trial. Level of Evidence: IV (Retrospective)

This study evaluates the short-term clinical and radiological outcomes of CD using the flip cutter technique of expandable reamer (ER), augmented with platelet-rich plasma (PRP) and calcium phosphate cement (CPC). Methods This uncontrolled retrospective single-centre observational study evaluated 25 hips in patients with symptomatic ARCO stage 1–2 AVNFH treated between January 2023 and January 2025. The surgical technique involved sequential debridement of necrotic bone through a minimal cortical window using ER, followed by PRP injection and sealing of the cortical defect with CPC. Patients were encouraged to bear weight immediately as tolerated. Outcomes were assessed in 6 weeks, and 3, 6, and 12 months using Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain scores, Harris Hip Scores (HHS), hip range of motion (ROM), and serial imaging, including a 1-year follow-up MRI. Results At the 12-month follow-up, the combined intervention was associated with a significant improvement in mean VAS pain scores, HHS and hip ROM (p < 0.05). Radiographic and MRI assessments confirmed no disease progression or subchondral collapse in any hip at one-year. The day-case procedure was performed safely with no recorded complications. Conclusion In this small retrospective study, ER-assisted core decompression with PRP and CPC was associated with improved short-term pain and functional scores, with no observed subchondral collapse or conversion to THA during approximately one year of follow-up. These findings should be interpreted as preliminary observations rather than evidence of definitive efficacy, and they require confirmation in adequately powered prospective comparative studies with longer-term follow-up. Novelty Statement By evaluating a tri-modal, minimally invasive technique combining expandable reamer debridement, platelet-rich plasma augmentation, and a calcium phosphate cement seal, this study provides preliminary evidence that this combined approach can potentially arrest disease progression and prevent subchondral collapse at one-year follow-up. Trial Registration: Not applicable, as this evaluation is based on retrospective clinical data and does not constitute a prospective healthcare trial. Level of Evidence: IV (Retrospective)

title: Multimodal MR Radiomics for Preoperative Prediction of Perineural Invasion and Prognostic Stratification in Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma
abstract: Abstract Background To develop and validate a multimodal model integrating multiphasic contrast-enhanced MRI radiomics with clinical-imaging information for the preoperative prediction of perineural invasion (PNI) in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) and for postoperative risk stratification. Methods Patients with ICC treated at the Eastern Hepatobiliary Surgery Hospital between September 2014 and February 2025 were retrospectively enrolled ( n = 455) and randomly assigned to training ( n = 232), testing ( n = 99) and validation ( n = 124) cohorts. Radiomic features were extracted with PyRadiomics from tumor regions on all four phases and selected by LASSO regression; the clinical-imaging, radiomics and multimodal models were built with logistic regression. Discrimination, calibration and clinical net benefit were assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). Overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) were compared by the Kaplan-Meier

title: Borderline Breast Phyllodes Tumor Coexisting with Intermediate- Grade Ductal Carcinoma In Situ and Focal Invasion: A Case Report and Literature Review
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Borderline phyllodes tumor (PT) coexisting with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) and invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) is an exceptionally rare mixed breast lesion. Due to its low incidence and compositional complexity, it poses substantial diagnostic and management challenges. We present such a case to highlight the pitfalls in preoperative diagnosis and the rationale for a multidisciplinary therapeutic strategy. Presentation of case: A 72-year-old Chinese female presented with a 2-week history of a right breast mass. Ultrasound and mammography revealed a large (52.6 mm), well-circumscribed, lobulated solid mass (BI-RADS 4A/4B), suggestive of a phyllodes tumor. Core needle biopsy returned “fibroadenoma with usual ductal hyperplasia.” Subsequent lumpectomy showed borderline PT (80%), intermediate-grade DCIS (20%), and focal Grade II invasive carcinoma of no special type (< 1%, maximal invasive diameter 3 mm). Immunohistochemistry of the invasive component: ER(−), PR(−), HER-2(3+), Ki-67 60%. Given the patient’s preference against breast conservation, a right total mastectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy was performed (0/1 nodes positive). Final staging: pT1aN0M0, Stage IA, HER-2 overexpression subtype. No adjuvant chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or radiotherapy was given. At 12-month follow-up, no local or distant recurrence was observed. Conclusion Definitive diagnosis of PT coexisting with DCIS and IDC relies on adequate excision specimens rather than biopsy alone. Clinical management should integrate PT behavior with standard breast cancer guidelines through multidisciplinary collaboration, balancing complete oncologic control against the risk of overtreatment. Longer follow-up is warranted to confirm durable outcomes.

title: A multimodal fusion model combining transfer-learning ultrasound deep features and clinical risk factors for predicting cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma: a multicentre retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Background Cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM) is the most common route of spread in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) and a key determinant of surgical extent, radioactive iodine therapy and recurrence risk. Pre-operative ultrasound has limited sensitivity for nodal disease, and objective, reproducible risk-stratification tools are needed. We developed and validated a multimodal model fusing deep ultrasound image features with clinical risk factors, compared it with clinical and image-only models, and evaluated its transportability in an independent external cohort. Methods In this multicentre retrospective study, 607 consecutive PTC patients (2022–2026; N1, 48.4%) with pre-operative grey-scale ultrasound and definitive histopathology were included, plus an external validation set of 252 consecutive patients (N1, 83.3%). Lesions were segmented by a YOLOv8-seg model trained on 390 manually labelled frames (mask mAP50 = 0.985), retaining 1,322 network-generated masks and making delineation operator-independent. The development cohort was split 7:3 into training (n = 424) and internal validation (n = 183) sets; univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified independent clinical risk factors. Ultrasound deep features (896-d pooled activations) were extracted by a same-domain transfer-pretrained backbone, reduced to 30 principal components and fused with clinical factors in a logistic regression head. Models were evaluated by AUC with bootstrap 95% CIs, DeLong tests, calibration curves, DCA and SHAP. Results Age (OR 0.959, 95% CI 0.936–0.982), female sex (OR 0.316, 0.178–0.564), tumour diameter (OR 5.321, 2.438–11.617), minimal extrathyroidal extension (OR 2.001, 1.071–3.741) and multifocality (OR 6.106, 2.178–17.118) were independent predictors. On internal validation, the clinical, ultrasound deep-learning and fusion models achieved AUCs of 0.709 (0.641–0.777), 0.642 (0.561–0.723) and 0.737 (0.665–0.808); the fusion model significantly outperformed the imaging model (dAUC = 0.094, P = 0.0015) and showed the highest net benefit on DCA. The clinical model showed limited transportability in the external validation set (n = 252; AUC = 0.528), consistent with case-mix-dependent shift. Conclusions Fusing same-domain transfer-learning ultrasound deep features with clinical risk factors achieved the highest internal-validation AUC and clinical net benefit, significantly outperforming image-only modelling; external validation of the fusion model remains to be performed. The same-domain transfer strategy offers a reproducible paradigm for small-sample medical imaging tasks.

title: Posterior cortical gray matter heterogeneity between hyposmia- and RBD-defined prodromal phenotypes in Parkinson's disease: a PPMI voxel-based morphometry study
abstract: Abstract Background Prodromal Parkinson's disease (PD) includes clinically distinct enrollment phenotypes. We examined whole-brain gray matter volume (GMV) in Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) participants recruited through hyposmia-only or REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD)-only pathways and assessed the stability of the findings. Methods Baseline T1-weighted MRI from 465 hyposmia-only and 149 RBD-only participants (N = 614) was analyzed with CAT12/SPM25 voxel-based morphometry (VBM). Models included age, sex, intracranial volume, and scanner family. Whole-brain clusters were defined at voxel p < 0.001 and tested using family-wise error (FWE) correction. We examined scanner-restricted samples, 123 sex/scanner-matched pairs, and 10,000-sign-flip permutation analysis of linear models (PALM). Bilateral cuneus/calcarine estimates and clinical assessments were exploratory. Results Whole-brain analysis identified a posterior phenotype effect (F cluster: k = 4,499; pFWE = 4.15×10⁻⁷), with higher GMV in hyposmia-only participants. In 123 matched pairs, a posterior H > RBD T cluster survived correction (pFWE = 0.0266), whereas the F contrast did not. PALM also identified a posterior effect (two-sided threshold-free cluster enhancement [TFCE] FWE p = 0.0027; voxelwise FWE p = 0.0277). Adjusted bilateral cuneus differences were + 0.211 mL (95% CI 0.095–0.327) in the full cohort and + 0.187 mL (0.041–0.333) after matching. MRI-proximal RBD screening questionnaire scores showed no significant association with regional GMV. Conclusions Posterior cortical GMV differed between these enrollment-defined prodromal phenotypes. The anatomical finding was supported by nonparametric inference, although the matched F test and strictest scanner restriction were nonsignificant. Longitudinal studies are needed to establish its clinical relevance.

title: Bilateral Gluteal Pyomyositis Caused by Citrobacter Species: A Case Report from Sudan
abstract: Abstract Background: Pyomyositis is a bacterial infection of skeletal muscle that most commonly affects tropical populations and is usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus . Gram-negative organisms are uncommon causes, and Citrobacter species are rarely reported. Case presentation: A 27-year-old Sudanese man with no known chronic medical illness presented with an 8-day history of high-grade fever followed by severe bilateral hip pain and gluteal swelling. Initial investigations showed leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and a positive typhoid IgM test, and ceftriaxone was initiated. During hospitalization, he developed progressive bilateral gluteal swelling, severe pain, and restricted hip movement. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated bilateral gluteal and peri-hip muscle inflammation with large intramuscular fluid collections consistent with pyomyositis. Image-guided aspiration yielded purulent material, from which Citrobacter species was isolated. Surgical drainage was recommended but declined by the patient. He was subsequently treated with repeated image-guided aspiration and two weeks of intravenous ciprofloxacin according to susceptibility testing, with marked clinical improvement and restoration of full hip movement. At three-week follow-up, he remained asymptomatic without clinical evidence of recurrence. Conclusion: Bilateral gram-negative pyomyositis caused by Citrobacter species is an unusual presentation in a previously healthy young adult. MRI and microbiological examination of aspirated material were important for diagnosis and targeted therapy. This case also illustrates that repeated percutaneous aspiration combined with appropriate antimicrobial therapy may provide an alternative source-control strategy when operative drainage is declined, although surgical or percutaneous drainage remains the recommended approach for established intramuscular abscesses.

title: A foundation model for three-dimensional anatomical reconstruction from sparse X-ray projections
abstract: Abstract Computed tomography (CT) provides three-dimensional anatomical information but requires costly scanners and exposes patients to higher radiation doses than conventional X-ray imaging. Reconstructing three-dimensional anatomy from a few X-ray projections could extend widely available X-ray systems beyond two-dimensional imaging. We present SPARC, a foundation model pretrained once on 47,149 chest scans across diverse acquisition settings, enabling a single model to be adapted to different X-ray imaging configurations and anatomical regions. Across eight datasets covering five body regions, seven mainly outside the chest, SPARC reconstructed volumes with greater fidelity than five existing methods, exceeding the strongest in peak signal-to-noise ratio by 0.8-2.6 dB with eight projections and 1.4-2.7 dB with four. CT-based tools for abnormality classification and organ segmentation retained most of their performance when applied directly to SPARC's reconstructions from eight projections, fewer than 3% of the hundreds recorded by a CT scanner. They reached 98% of their area under the receiver operating characteristic curve on CT for 18 chest abnormalities, and 86% and 93% of their Dice score on CT for abdominal organs and lung lobes, with Dice scores 8.8% and 4.4% higher, in relative terms, than with the best competing method. Pretraining considerably increased the adaptation data efficiency. With ten patients, SPARC reconstructed chest CT more accurately than the same architecture trained from scratch on 100 patients. With the models and code released, SPARC could support the clinical translation of sparse-view reconstruction and expand access to three-dimensional imaging where CT scanners are unavailable.

title: Feasibility of chronic kidney disease classification using bilateral kidney ultrasound and foundation model representations
abstract: Abstract Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health burden, yet early diagnosis remains challenging and conventional kidney ultrasonography is limited by operator dependence and low sensitivity to subtle textural changes. We investigated the feasibility of an ultrasound foundation model for CKD classification from bilateral kidney ultrasound images, with reference labels defined using an operational subset of the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) 2024 guidelines. In this retrospective single-center study, 13,245 kidney ultrasound images from 1,484 patients (1,128 with CKD and 356 without) were analyzed. The Universal Ultrasound Foundation Model (USFM) was compared with five fine-tuned deep learning architectures (VGG16, ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, EfficientNet-B0, and Vision Transformer) over 10 random seeds, with performance assessed at the sample and examination levels. USFM achieved the highest mean values for most metrics, although its confidence intervals overlapped with those of the strongest baseline, and it showed greater stability across repeated experiments. At the examination level, it achieved a balanced accuracy of 74.49 ± 4.63\%, an F1-score of 73.59 ± 3.60\%, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 84.80 ± 1.98\%, with comparable results at the sample level. These findings support the feasibility of ultrasound foundation models for CKD classification from bilateral kidney ultrasound images and motivate external validation.

title: Dual-Wield: An Observational Study of Utilization and Outcomes of Cryobiopsy and Intraoperative CT scan During Navigational Bronchoscopy
abstract: Abstract Background Pulmonary nodules are common incidental imaging findings, and distinguishing malignant from benign etiologies frequently requires invasive sampling. CT-guided transthoracic needle biopsy offers high yield but carries pneumothorax rates of 15–45% and precludes concurrent mediastinal staging. Shape-sensing navigational bronchoscopy, intraprocedural cone-beam CT (CBCT), and transbronchial cryobiopsy have each independently improved bronchoscopy performance, but integration of all three into one workflow remains poorly characterized. We describe real-world utilization and outcomes of these modalities at a large volume community tertiary care center. Research Question What is the real-world utilization, diagnostic performance, and complication rate of navigational bronchoscopy for lung nodule sampling with the addition of CBCT and cryobiopsy? Study Design and Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of navigational bronchoscopy procedures performed at a single community tertiary care center between January 1, 2024, and January 1, 2026. Two physician investigators independently abstracted procedure reports, imaging, and pathology from the electronic health record, recording cryobiopsy use, CBCT use, target nodule size, pathology, and complications. Diagnostic yield was determined using the strict ATS/ACCP consensus definition. Results Among 199 navigational bronchoscopy procedures, 229 lesions were sampled. Mean nodule size was 22.4 ± 17.7 mm overall, smallest with cryobiopsy plus CBCT (17.4 ± 13.7 mm) and largest with no adjunctive modality (29.8 ± 20.3 mm). Overall diagnostic yield was 78.0%: 83.9% with cryobiopsy plus CBCT, 75.0% cryobiopsy alone, 70.4% CBCT alone, and 73.2% no adjunctive modality. The complication rate was 3.5% (7/199). Diagnostic yield trended higher in cases with both cryobiopsy and CBCT. Conclusion Integrating navigational bronchoscopy with CBCT and cryobiopsy achieved the highest diagnostic yield while sampling the smallest nodules with an acceptable safety profile. Prospective randomized studies are warranted to define the independent contribution of each adjunct and to detect any true incremental harm.

title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Volumetric Quantification of Urinary Stone Burden and Hydronephrosis From CT Images
abstract: Abstract Purpose Given the limitations of conventional stone burden assessment based on maximum diameter or ellipsoid-derived volume estimates, we aimed to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)–based method for automated quantification of stone and hydronephrosis volumes from CT images. Materials and Methods A 2-step algorithm was developed. First, a U-Net incorporating residual blocks, dense blocks, a morphology-aware block, and attention gates (RDAM U-Net) segmented the kidneys; hyperparameters were optimized using Complex System Response (CSR) experimental design with 5-fold cross-validation. Second, within the segmented kidney, hydronephrosis was identified from low–Hounsfield unit (HU) regions, and renal stones from high-HU regions using morphological processing and 3-dimensional (3D) connected-component analysis. AI-derived stone volumes were compared with ellipsoid-based estimates using Pearson and Spearman correlation, Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and Bland–Altman analysis. Results Eighty-two kidney CT cases were used for model development. RDAM U-Net achieved a mean intersection over union of 0.9432 and Dice coefficient of 0.9681, with fewer parameters and a 32.58% shorter parameter-update time than reference attention-based U-Nets. In 39 paired stone measurements, AI-derived and ellipsoid-estimated volumes showed a near-perfect correlation (Pearson r = 0.977; Spearman ρ = 0.966; R² = 0.954; all p < 0.001) and high agreement (Lin's CCC = 0.959; ICC = 0.960).
