title: Explainable, Uncertainty-Aware Ensemble Learning for Brain Tumor Classification from MRI with a Simulated Fairness Audit
abstract: Abstract Most brain MRI classifiers stop at accuracy; whether their explanations hold up, how sure each call is and whether some patients fare worse is rarely checked. We combined five convolutional networks (Xception, InceptionV3, EfficientNetB4, DenseNet121 and ConvNeXtTiny) and a ViT-B/16 transformer through a logistic regression meta-learner fitted on Out-of-Fold predictions. The models were trained with five-fold cross-validation on 5,040 of 7,200 class-balanced MRI images and tested once on 1,080 held-out images. The MetaEnsemble reached 98.33% accuracy, an AUC-ROC of 0.9989 and an Expected Calibration Error of 0.0083, whereas every single model was underconfident. We set LIME, SHAP, Grad-CAM and Grad-CAM + + side by side and scored the Grad-CAM maps (localization accuracy, Pointing Game accuracy, AOPC faithfulness) instead of judging them by eye. Forty Monte Carlo Dropout passes per image gave each case an uncertainty estimate. Lacking patient metadata, we simulated age and sex labels from epidemiological priors to demonstrate a fairness audit; the gaps were small but pointed the same way in every model (age 1.55% to 4.00%, sex 1.07% to 2.05%). The evidence comes from one public dataset, but it shows that explanation scoring, uncertainty estimation and subgroup checks can be planned into a brain tumor classifier from the start.

title: Single-Projection Three-Dimensional X-ray Imaging through Time- and Energy-Resolved Photon Scattering
abstract: Abstract Scattered X-ray photons contain information about material composition but are generally treated as contamination in conventional computed tomography (CT). We investigate a theoretical time- and energy-encoded CT framework that uses photon arrival time, position, and energy to localize scattering events and reconstruct three-dimensional Rayleigh and Compton scattering distributions from a single projection without mechanical rotation. The framework was evaluated using Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations of heterogeneous tissue, head-and-neck, and high-resolution pattern phantoms. Under idealized source and detector conditions, the reconstructed scattering distributions differentiated soft tissues and reproduced simulated structures, including features as small as 0.1 mm. Quantitative errors of approximately 1–7% and a simulated dose of 50 µGy were reported for the investigated configurations. These results establish the information-reconstruction potential of time- and energy-resolved scatter measurements, rather than the performance of a realizable clinical scanner. Implementation will require ultrashort X-ray pulses, precise photon timing and energy measurements, and adequate detector coverage. The approach provides a theoretical basis for investigating single-projection volumetric X-ray scatter imaging and material characterization.

title: Prediction of Lymphovascular Invasion in Breast Cancer Using Intratumoral and Peritumoral MRI Radiomics Models Based on DCE-MRI: A Multicenter Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose This study explores the predictive value of intramural and peritumoral radiomics features based on dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) for lymphovascular invasion (LVI) in breast cancer. It compares the predictive efficacy of different peritumoral regions and feature fusion methods, and constructs a combined prediction model integrating clinical characteristics. Materials and Methods Retrospectively collected images from 757 breast cancer patients with pathologically confirmed diagnoses who underwent breast DCE-MRI examinations at two medical centers. Data from Center 1 served as the training set (n = 529), while data from Center 2 formed the external validation set (n = 228). Tumor lesions were semi-automatically delineated using ITK-SNAP software, with peritumoral regions automatically expanded. Regions of interest (ROIs) were selected on the maximum intensity phase of DCE-MRI. Radiomics features were extracted using PyRadiomics across four modalities: intratumoral, peritumoral (1mm, 3mm, 5mm, 7mm, 10mm, 15mm, 20mm), Tumor+Peri7mm, and ImageFusion7 (a fusion of tumor and optimal 7mm peritumoral regions). Data dimensionality reduction and feature selection were performed using Spearman correlation analysis, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression, and Maximum Relevance-Minimum Redundancy (mRMR) methods. Five classifiers—support vector machine (SVM), extreme trees (ET), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and multilayer perceptron (MLP)—were evaluated under different feature models to identify the optimal classifier for constructing the radiomics model. Clinical Features: Single- and multi-factor logistic regression screened clinical risk factors to construct a clinical model. Comprehensive evaluations were conducted on the clinical model, the optimal radiomic model, and a combined model incorporating clinical features with optimal radiomic features. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves analyzed predictive performance, with area under the curve (AUC) calculated. A fusion model was established by integrating the radiomic score (rad-score) from the highest-performing predictive model and visualized via a nomogram. The clinical utility of the predictive models was assessed using calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Clinical characteristics: The AUC values of the clinical model based on histological grade, sentinel lymph node status, and TIC were 0.738 (95% CI: 0.6949–0.7802) and 0.749 (95% CI: 0.6830–0.8141) in the training and validation sets, respectively. As a key indicator reflecting lymph node metastasis in primary tumors, sentinel lymph node status is widely recognized for its role in breast cancer staging and prognostic assessment. For instance, in breast cancer, the area under the ROC curve for a non-sentinel lymph node metastasis risk prediction model in sentinel lymph node-positive patients reached 0.7613, demonstrating its clinical utility. Radiomics: Among the various peritumoral models, the 7 mm peritumoral model demonstrated the best performance. Results indicate that the radiomics model based on the ImageFusion7 (intra-tumor and peritumoral image fusion region) demonstrated optimal diagnostic performance, with the XGBoost classifier showing particularly outstanding results: an AUC of 0.861 (95% CI: 0.8302–0.8914) in the training set and an AUC of 0.709 (95% CI: 0.6407–0.7768). When constructing a clinical-imaging fusion model, the ROC curve based on clinical features and Radscore values achieved AUC values of 0.892 (95% CI: 0.8629–0.9165) and 0.778 (95% CI: 0.7140–0.8375) in the training and validation sets, respectively, surpassing all single models and the intra-tumoral/peritumoral model. The DCA curve demonstrated that the combined model exhibited the highest clinical efficacy and closely followed the diagonal line in the calibration curve, indicating superior model fit and generalization capability. Conclusions An image-based model utilizing DCE-MRI effectively predicts lymphovascular invasion (LVI) status in breast cancer, with the ImageFusion7 model—which integrates images from both the tumor interior and a 7mm peritumoral region—demonstrating optimal predictive performance. Combining this model with clinically independent risk factors further enhances its accuracy. The constructed fusion model exhibits strong discriminatory power and clinical applicability, providing a valuable tool for non-invasive preoperative assessment of LVI risk.

title: Pulmonary artery intimal sarcoma misdiagnosed as pulmonary embolism: MDM2 amplification as the diagnostic anchor in an unresectable tumor—a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Pulmonary artery intimal sarcoma (PAIS) is a rare and aggressive vascular malignancy whose clinical and radiological features overlap with those of pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE); most patients are initially anticoagulated, and no standard systemic therapy exists for unresectable disease. Amplification of MDM2 is the defining genomic event, yet it is usually treated as a supplementary finding rather than as a diagnostic test. Case presentation A 51-year-old man without thromboembolic risk factors presented with cough, sputum production, and chest discomfort. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) showed filling defects extending from the main pulmonary artery into both branches together with a 5.0 × 2.7 cm left upper lobe mass, and he received rivaroxaban until hemoptysis occurred. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET)/CT showed concordant hypermetabolism of the intravascular and parenchymal lesions. Two biopsies, including an expert review, narrowed the differential only to intimal sarcoma versus sarcomatoid carcinoma; next-generation sequencing then identified MDM2 amplification with CDKN2A deletion, a low tumor mutational burden (1.95 mutations/Mb), and negative PD-L1 expression, establishing MDM2-driven PAIS. Because the tumor was unresectable, he received six cycles of sintilimab, docetaxel, and cisplatin, two further cycles of sintilimab and docetaxel, consolidative intensity-modulated radiotherapy (60 Gy in 25 fractions), and maintenance sintilimab monotherapy. The best response was stable disease with a 27.9% reduction in the sum of target-lesion diameters, and progression-free survival reached 12.1 months without grade ≥3 immune-related adverse events. Conclusions When morphology and immunohistochemistry are indeterminate, MDM2 amplification can be the decisive diagnostic test rather than a supplementary finding, and it should be sought before empirical treatment is committed. Chemotherapy-primed PD-1 blockade followed by consolidative radiotherapy produced durable disease control in an immunologically cold tumor; prospective registries are needed to test this sequence.

title: Parameter-Efficient Mask-Conditioned Magnetic Resonance Image Synthesis for Segmentation Augmentation
abstract: Abstract When real training images for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation are limited, existing masks can be reused to synthesize additional image appearances. However, paired image-translation methods may favor pixel fidelity over distributional similarity, while full diffusion-model fine-tuning is costly and generic conditioning does not explicitly encode mask geometry. To address these limitations, we propose ControlNet-guided Low-Rank Adaptation for MRI synthesis (\method), a mask-conditioned latent diffusion framework that adapts both the denoising and spatial-conditioning pathways. Only 2.96\% of the framework parameters are trainable in the BraTS configuration. We evaluate image quality and segmentation utility on BraTS2020 brain MRI and ACDC cardiac MRI across four fractions of real training slices. On BraTS T1 contrast-enhanced MRI, \method achieves a lower FID than Pix2Pix (55.65 versus 162.42), although Pix2Pix has higher paired pixel fidelity. With 10\% real training slices, adding synthetic pairs raises mean Dice from 0.7208 to 0.7401 and reduces HD95 from 48.43 to 45.34 pixels in a within-cohort, slice-level BraTS evaluation. On 50 held-out ACDC patients, a separately trained adapter raises mean Dice from 0.7661 to 0.8263 and reduces HD95 from 15.40 to 13.63 pixels at the same fraction. Gains diminish as real-image availability increases. These results support targeted use of parameter-efficient, mask-conditioned MRI synthesis when real-image coverage is low.

title: Interpretable multimodal deep learning for diagnosis and symptom-onset prediction in genetic frontotemporal dementia
abstract: Abstract Background: Genetic frontotemporal dementia (FTD) is characterized by substantial clinical and neuroanatomical heterogeneity, making prediction of symptom onset challenging. We evaluated whether deep learning-derived MRI biomarkers could be combined with non-imaging biomarkers in an interpretable framework for diagnosis and phenoconversion prediction in genetic FTD. Methods: We evaluated Multi-ICNN, a multimodal extension of the Interpretable Convolutional Neural Network, using data from the FTD Risk Cohort. Imaging biomarkers derived from T1-weighted MRI were combined with demographic, genetic, and neuropsychological biomarkers in an additive prediction model. We evaluated classification of symptomatic mutation carriers versus genetically confirmed non-carriers and phenoconversion prediction within 2- and 5-year time horizons. Biomarker contributions were examined at the group and participant levels. Results: For diagnosis, Multi-ICNN achieved the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.953, numerically outperforming the single-modality models. For phenoconversion prediction, the deep learning-based models outperformed the conventional volumetric and non-imaging models. The imaging-only ICNN achieved the highest mean AUCs of 0.798 and 0.780 for the 2- and 5-year horizons, respectively. Adding non-imaging biomarkers did not further improve ICNN performance. Neuropsychological measures contributed most strongly to diagnosis, whereas imaging-derived biomarkers dominated phenoconversion prediction, particularly biomarkers involving frontal and temporal regions. The additive model also provided participant-specific biomarker contributions. Conclusions: Interpretable deep learning-derived MRI biomarkers showed promise for phenoconversion prediction in genetic FTD, while the value of multimodal integration depended on the clinical task. The main limitations were the modest sample size and lack of external validation, reflecting the rarity of genetic FTD and the limited availability of comparable longitudinal cohorts.

title: High burden of treatment-requiring retinopathy of prematurity in Kathmandu, Nepal: a prospective multicentre observational study
abstract: Abstract Background: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is an important cause of avoidable childhood blindness in low- and middle-income countries, where increasing survival of preterm infants has outpaced improvements in neonatal care. We assessed the frequency, severity and treatment requirements of ROP across neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) and specialist eye centres in the Kathmandu Valley. Methods: This prospective multi-centre observational cohort study was conducted from February–November 2025 at two level III NICUs and two tertiary eye centres in Kathmandu. Preterm infants with a gestational age (GA) <34 weeks and/or a birth weight (BW) <2000 g, and infants of 34–36 weeks GA with risk factors, were enrolled. Bilateral wide-field retinal imaging was performed at serial examinations and ROP was classified according to ICROP-3. The primary outcome was development of type 1 ROP. Baseline characteristics were compared between infants who developed type 1 ROP and those with type 2 ROP or no ROP using t-tests and chi-square tests, with odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for factors estimated for prespecified factors associated with type 1 ROP. Results: Of 222 infants who underwent at least one ROP examination, 208 completed follow-up to complete retinal vascularisation or disease resolution. Among these 208 infants, 76 (36.5%) developed ROP, including 46 (22.1%) with type 1 ROP and 30 (14.4%) with type 2 ROP. Aggressive posterior ROP (A-ROP) occurred in 14 (6.7%) infants. Infants who developed type 1 ROP had lower mean GA and BW than those with type 2 ROP or no ROP. BW ≤1500 g was associated with type 1 ROP (OR 2.99, 95% CI 1.73–5.18). Type 1 ROP was more frequently observed among infants screened at specialist eye centres than NICUs (OR 3.12, 95% CI 1.67–5.80), although this comparison may reflect referral selection. ROP was present at the first examination in 60 of 222 infants (27.0%). 3/25 infants (12.0%) outside the principal enrollment thresholds developed ROP, including 1/25 (4.0%) with type 1 ROP. Conclusions: ROP, including Type 1 disease, was frequently observed, with some cases detected at the initial screening and among infants beyond conventional eligibility criteria, underscoring the need for Nepal-specific screening guidelines and strengthened referral pathways. title: Quantitative MRI Morphometry Predicts Functional Disability in Patients with Lumbar Spinal Stenosis: A Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Background: To evaluate the association between magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings, lumbar spine morphometric parameters, and functional disability in patients with lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS). Methods: In this retrospective observational study, patients with MRI-confirmed LSS were evaluated using axial T2-weighted MRI. Imaging findings, including central stenosis, lateral recess stenosis (LRS), facet joint effusion (FJE), and sedimentation sign, were assessed. Quantitative morphometric measurements of the dural sac, spinal canal, and lateral recess were obtained. Functional disability was evaluated using the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Associations between MRI findings, morphometric parameters, ODI scores, and symptom categories were analyzed. Results: Central stenosis and LRS were significantly associated with higher ODI scores and symptom categories (both p < 0.0001), whereas FJE and the sedimentation sign showed no significant associations. ODI demonstrated significant negative correlations with total spinal canal cross-sectional area ( r = −0.6965), dural sac cross-sectional area ( r = −0.6549), and transverse dural sac diameter ( r = −0.5863). Morphometric threshold analysis identified severe stenosis at a dural sac cross-sectional area <0.201 cm² and a total spinal canal cross-sectional area <0.04 cm². Conclusions: Quantitative MRI morphometric parameters demonstrated significant associations with functional disability in patients with LSS. Objective measurements of the dural sac and spinal canal may complement conventional MRI grading and assist in evaluating disease severity and clinical decision-making.

title: Compact CNN--Transformer Refinement for Patient-Disjoint Brain Tumor MRI Classification with an Optimized CNN Comparator
abstract: Abstract Hybrid CNN--Transformer classifiers can appear advantageous when compared only with fixed or untuned CNN baselines, making it difficult to separate the effect of global-context refinement from hyperparameter optimization and imbalance handling. This study evaluates a compact EfficientNet-B0--Transformer against a matched-budget optimized CNN-only comparator using 3,064 contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI slices from 233 patients. All model development used patient-disjoint training, validation, and held-out test partitions. The CNN-only and hybrid pipelines used focal loss and adaptive minority-class augmentation and were independently optimized with 40 Optuna tree-structured Parzen estimator trials; the test set remained inaccessible during selection. On the held-out set, optimized CNN and hybrid models achieved Macro F1 scores of 0.9096 and 0.9341, respectively, with patient Macro F1 of 0.8956 and 0.9327. Across three independent training seeds, hybrid image-level Macro F1 was 0.9249 ± 0.0187 versus 0.9018 ± 0.0090 for the optimized CNN. However, patient-wise five-fold robustness results were close (0.9355 ± 0.0383 versus 0.9342 ± 0.0455), and the paired patient-level McNemar test was not significant (p=0.5). The hybrid required only 9.5% more parameters, with modest latency and memory overhead. The results support compact self-attention as an incremental refinement, while showing that its benefit should be judged against equally optimized CNN baselines and multiple robustness checks.

title: Complement C1q drives skeletal muscle wasting in pancreatic cancer
abstract: Abstract Cancer cachexia, defined by involuntary skeletal muscle loss, affects ~ 70% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients at diagnosis and independently worsens survival. Here, we identify complement component 1q (C1q) as a driver of PDAC-induced muscle wasting, with coordinated effects across muscle, tumor, and systemic inflammatory compartments. In cachectic PDAC patient muscle, C1q partially co-deposits with IgM, and C1q mRNA correlates with reduced muscle radiation attenuation, a CT-derived measure of muscle quality. In PDAC tumors, C1q protein correlates with immunosuppressive programs and independently predicts poor survival. These findings are recapitulated in orthotopic KPC mice, where C1q mRNA is upregulated in respiratory muscle before cachexia onset, and C1q deposits in tumors and co-deposits with IgM in muscles of cachectic mice. C1qa deletion reduced systemic inflammatory mediators, blocked muscle atrophy, and improved activity and grip strength in KPC mice, while attenuating immune cell infiltration and extracellular matrix remodeling in respiratory muscle. Host C1qa deletion also suppressed angiogenic and immunosuppressive programs in KPC tumors, while increasing intratumoral CD8⁺ T cell density and Granzyme B production. These findings position C1q as a driver of cancer-induced muscle wasting and tumor immunosuppression, supporting C1q inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy targeting pathological features of poor-prognosis PDAC.

title: Intraoperative Renal Biopsy During Liver Transplantation in Patients with Preexisting Acute Kidney Injury: Histopathological Associations with Postoperative Renal Replacement Therapy
abstract: Abstract Background. Acute kidney injury (AKI) in decompensated cirrhosis is associated with poor outcomes after liver transplantation (LT), and creatinine-based tools poorly predict postoperative renal recovery. We evaluated whether histopathology on intraoperative renal biopsy is associated with renal replacement therapy (RRT) after LT. Methods. In this retrospective single-center cohort study, 22 adults with decompensated cirrhosis and KDIGO-defined AKI underwent intraoperative renal biopsy during deceased-donor LT between October 2022 and June 2024. Two early deaths were retained in the safety cohort, leaving 20 patients for renal-outcome analysis. The primary endpoint was RRT within 90 days; prespecified histological predictors were acute tubular injury (ATI) score ≥ 2 and interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (IFTA) > 10%. Results. Five of 20 patients (25.0%) initiated RRT within 90 days, and 3 remained RRT-dependent at day 90. RRT occurred in 5 of 9 patients with ATI ≥ 2 versus 0 of 11 with ATI < 2 (risk difference, 55.6 percentage points; 95% CI, 16.8–81.1; P = .008) and in 4 of 7 with IFTA > 10% versus 1 of 13 with IFTA ≤ 10% (risk difference, 49.5 percentage points; 95% CI, 8.4–77.2; P = .031). IFTA correlated strongly with time to renal function stabilization (Spearman ρ = 0.907; P < .001). No severe biopsy-related complications occurred, although transient hematuria was common. No conventional preoperative clinical variable distinguished patients with and without subsequent RRT. Conclusions. Moderate-to-severe ATI and IFTA burden on intraoperative renal biopsy were associated with post-LT RRT requirement. Intraoperative biopsy was feasible in this high-risk population. These hypothesis-generating findings require validation in larger multicenter cohorts.

title: Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices Toward Breast Cancer Among Nursing and Midwifery Students at the University of Health Sciences, Cambodia
abstract: Abstract Background Breast cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer among Cambodian women, with an estimated 2,116 new cases and 917 deaths in 2022. Nurses and midwives deliver most primary care in Cambodia, yet evidence on the knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) of students in these professions toward breast cancer is lacking. This study assessed breast cancer KAP among nursing and midwifery students in Cambodia. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted in November 2024 among 705 students enrolled in four nursing and midwifery programmes at the University of Health Sciences, Phnom Penh. A structured, self-administered 50-item questionnaire assessed knowledge (25 items), attitudes (16 items) and breast self-examination (BSE) practice (3 items). Data were analysed using Pearson’s chi-square tests, Welch two-sample t-tests, one-way analysis of variance and Pearson correlation. Results Overall, 73.3% of students had adequate knowledge, 99.7% held positive attitudes and 85.2% were classified as having good BSE practice. Knowledge, attitude and practice scores differed significantly by year of study (p < 0.001), with mean knowledge scores increasing from 13.9 in Year 1 to 19.7 in Year 4. Knowledge and attitude scores did not differ between programmes, whereas midwifery students more often reported practising BSE than nursing students (88.2% vs. 66.4%, p < 0.001). Only 45.1% had heard of mammography and 56.3% recognised a painless lump as a warning sign, while 48.1% believed that breast cancer is fatal for all patients. Knowledge correlated moderately with attitude (r = 0.425) and practice (r = 0.400) (both p < 0.001). Conclusions Nursing and midwifery students held favourable attitudes toward early detection, but important gaps persisted in mammography awareness, recognition of a painless lump as a warning sign and identification of hormonal and lifestyle risk factors. Integrating structured breast health education, including clinical breast examination skills, early in pre-service curricula may strengthen the capacity of this workforce to support early detection of breast cancer in Cambodia.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Automated Detection and Segmentation of Pulp Stones in Cone Beam Computed Tomography Scans.
abstract: Abstract Objective : This study aimed to automatically detect the human tooth pulp cavity and pulp stones on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) using deep learning-based semantic segmentation. Methodology : 523 annotated images of teeth from 112 CBCT examinations were used to train and evaluate four established deep learning architectures (U-Net, Attention U-Net, U-Net++, and DeepLabV3+) in segmenting the background, pulp cavity, and pulp stone(s). Subsequently a novel architecture was developed (DACA-DeepLab) and evaluated through an additive study. DACA-DeepLab incorporates DeepLabV3+ with a pyramid channel-spatial attention (PCSA) module, a dual-axis cross-attention (DACA) decoder, and a Sobel-guided boundary-refinement (BFR) head. Results : DeepLabV3+ achieved the best overall Dice performance among the four baseline architectures (mean, 0.775; pulp cavity, 0.838; pulp stone, 0.711). In the second study, combining PCSA and DACA yielded the highest performance (mean Dice, 0.733). Adding the boundary-refinement head reduced performance, suggesting sensitivity to the limited training set. Conclusion : Deep learning-based semantic segmentation can accurately identify human tooth pulp cavity and pulp stone(s) on CBCT. These findings establish a systematic benchmark for CBCT-based pulp segmentation and provide a foundation for AI-assisted endodontic diagnosis and pre-treatment planning.

title: Development and characterization of FI 7500: a novel near-infrared dye for in vitro and in vivo cell labeling
abstract: Abstract Near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent dyes offer considerable advantages over visible-light fluorescent dyes for in vivo imaging, including reduced tissue scattering and superior penetration depth. Current in vivo imaging in small animals predominantly relies on bioluminescence imaging using luciferase-expressing cells, which requires genetic modification and repeated substrate administration. However, only a few NIR fluorescent dyes have been sufficiently validated for in vivo applications. Here, we present a comprehensive characterization of the NIR fluorescent dye FI 7500 as a practical alternative to bioluminescence imaging. Microscopy-based analysis revealed that FI 7500 specifically localizes to the cytoplasm across multiple cell types, enabling clear visualization of cellular morphology in both two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) culture models. In 3D spheroid imaging, FI 7500 visualized the internal structures of live spheroids containing up to 2×10 3 cells, and optical clearing extended visualization to spheroids containing 1×10 4 cells. Furthermore, FI 7500 enabled clear surface imaging and delineation of individual cells regardless of spheroid size. In vivo, subcutaneously transplanted FI 7500-stained cells retained fluorescence for up to 21 days, with minimal effects on tumor growth. After intravenous administration, FI 7500-stained lung-metastasizing cells accumulated in the lungs, consistent with the bioluminescence signal after luciferin administration. These findings support the use of FI 7500 as a versatile and reliable tool for cellular and in vivo imaging, expanding the choice of validated NIR dyes and providing essential data to guide probe selection for specific experimental applications.

title: Value of 18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics combined with clinical features for predicting Ki-67 expression in colorectal cancer
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the value of 18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics combined with clinical features for the preoperative prediction of Ki-67 expression in colorectal cancer (CRC). Methods A total of 117 patients with pathologically confirmed CRC who underwent pretreatment 18F-FDG PET/CT between June 2016 and October 2024 were retrospectively included. Patients were classified into high- and low-expression groups using a 50% Ki-67 cutoff and were randomly divided into a training cohort and an internal validation cohort at a 7:3 ratio. Radiomic features were extracted from CT and PET images and reduced by standardization, univariate screening, correlation analysis, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), ExtraTrees, LightGBM, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifiers were compared. Independent clinical predictors were identified to construct a clinical model and a combined clinical-radiomics nomogram. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, the DeLong test, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Six CT features, four PET features, and ten combined PET/CT features were retained. TNM stage, SUVmax, and SUVmean were independent predictors of high Ki-67 expression. The LightGBM-based PET/CT radiomics model achieved AUCs of 0.943 and 0.911 in the training and internal validation cohorts, respectively, with an accuracy of 0.861 in the validation cohort. The combined nomogram achieved AUCs of 0.951 and 0.913, with validation-cohort accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score of 0.917, 0.920, 0.909, and 0.939, respectively. The AUC difference between the combined model and the PET/CT radiomics model was not statistically significant, whereas DCA showed a higher net benefit for the combined model within part of the clinically relevant threshold range. Conclusion Multimodal 18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics characterizes CRC from complementary morphologic and metabolic perspectives. Combining radiomics with TNM stage and conventional metabolic parameters may improve preoperative identification of high Ki-67 expression. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

The LightGBM-based PET/CT radiomics model achieved AUCs of 0.943 and 0.911 in the training and internal validation cohorts, respectively, with an accuracy of 0.861 in the validation cohort. The combined nomogram achieved AUCs of 0.951 and 0.913, with validation-cohort accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score of 0.917, 0.920, 0.909, and 0.939, respectively. The AUC difference between the combined model and the PET/CT radiomics model was not statistically significant, whereas DCA showed a higher net benefit for the combined model within part of the clinically relevant threshold range. Conclusion Multimodal 18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics characterizes CRC from complementary morphologic and metabolic perspectives. Combining radiomics with TNM stage and conventional metabolic parameters may improve preoperative identification of high Ki-67 expression. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Diagnostic yield of Virtual Bronchoscopic Navigation (VBN) guided Bronchoalveolar Lavage (BAL) in peripheral pulmonary infections: a prospective pilot study
abstract: Abstract Background: Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) is a key diagnostic tool in evaluating pulmonary infections and infiltrative lung diseases. However, conventional BAL relies on operator-dependent segment selection, potentially limiting diagnostic yield in peripheral pulmonary lesions. Virtual Bronchoscopic Navigation (VBN) has been shown to improve localization in biopsy procedures but its role in guiding BAL remains unexplored. Objectives: To evaluate the diagnostic yield of VBN-guided BAL in patients with clinical features of pulmonary infection having peripheral pulmonary lesions on radiology. Methods: This prospective observational pilot study included 50 adult patients with features of pulmonary infection having peripheral pulmonary lesions on radiology. All patients underwent VBN-guided BAL. Samples were analyzed using microbiological, molecular, and cytological techniques. Diagnostic yield and impact on clinical diagnosis were assessed. Results: A definitive diagnosis was achieved in 42/50 patients (84%). Diagnostic yield was higher in immunocompromised patients (92.9%) compared to non-immunocompromised patients (80.6%), though not statistically significant (p=0.414). The final diagnosis differed from the initial clinical diagnosis in 62% of cases. Common diagnoses included bacterial pneumonia (36%), tuberculosis (28%), and fungal infections (16%). Conclusion: VBN-guided BAL demonstrates high diagnostic yield in peripheral pulmonary lesions and may significantly alter clinical management. Larger comparative studies are required to validate these findings.

title: Analysis of Risk Factors and Establishment of a Predictive Model for Endplate Collapse After Posterior Short-Segment Fixation Combined with Screw Placement at the Injured Vertebra in Thoracolumbar Fractures
abstract: Abstract Purpose To identify the risk factors for endplate collapse in patients with thoracolumbar fractures undergoing posterior short-segment fixation combined with intermediate screw placement, and to develop and validate a clinical prediction model to aid in early risk stratification and prognosis optimization. Materials and methods Clinical data from 135 patients with thoracolumbar fractures treated with posterior short-segment fixation and screw placement at the injured vertebra were retrospectively analyzed. Based on postoperative imaging findings, patients were stratified into an endplate collapse group (n = 57) and a non-collapse control group (n = 78). Variables collected included demographic and fracture characteristics (age, gender, BMI, fracture location, fracture pattern, mechanism of injury, osteoporotic status), radiographic parameters (screw length at the injured vertebra, severity of endplate and intervertebral disc injury, extent of anterior and posterior complex injury, postoperative mean vertebral body height [MVBH] and Cobb angle [CA]), and postoperative outcomes (fixation duration, postoperative Pfirrmann grade). Univariate analysis identified variables with significant between-group differences. Independent risk factors for postoperative endplate collapse were determined by multivariable logistic regression analysis. A predictive model was constructed incorporating these factors, and its performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis with calculation of area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity. Results Univariate analysis revealed significant differences in BMI, osteoporotic status, screw depth, endplate injury grade, intervertebral disc injury severity (Sander classification), load-sharing classification (LSC) score, postoperative Pfirrmann grade, and postoperative Cobb angle between groups (all P < 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression identified osteoporosis, screw depth, and endplate injury grade as independent risk factors for postoperative endplate collapse (all P < 0.05), with screw depth demonstrating the largest odds ratio and thus the strongest association. A predictive model incorporating these three factors was constructed. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis demonstrated an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.888 (95% CI: 0.826–0.943), with sensitivity of 78.9% and specificity of 89.7%, indicating favorable predictive performance. Conclusion Postoperative endplate collapse following posterior short-segment fixation with injured vertebra screw placement for thoracolumbar fractures is multifactorial, with osteoporosis, screw depth, and endplate injury grade serving as major independent risk factors. The predictive model developed in this study effectively stratifies the risk of postoperative endplate collapse and may provide a valuable tool for preoperative risk assessment, intraoperative technical optimization, and postoperative individualized rehabilitation planning, thereby potentially reducing the incidence of endplate collapse and improving functional outcomes.

title: Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy and Metabolic MRI in Epilepsy: A Systematic Review and Quantitative Synthesis of Neurochemical Biomarkers and Clinical Applications
abstract: Abstract Background: Since the introduction of proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (¹H-MRS) in epilepsy research in the 1980s, metabolic MRI has provided unique insights into the neurochemical alterations underlying epilepsy. However, evidence has remained fragmented across imaging modalities, epilepsy syndromes, and clinical applications. We systematically reviewed the literature to define the metabolic phenotype of epilepsy and evaluate the evolving role of metabolic MRI in epilepsy research and clinical practice. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed and Scopus were systematically searched through April 2026 for original human studies investigating metabolic MRI in epilepsy. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment. Findings were synthesized through structured qualitative evidence, supported by integrated methodological, scientometric, tabular, and visual analyses. Results: A total of 298 studies were included. Focal epilepsy demonstrated widespread alterations involving N-acetyl aspartate, glutamate, Gamma-aminobutyric acid, choline-containing compounds, myo-inositol, lactate, and other metabolites across epileptogenic and brain networks. Generalized epilepsy was characterized by predominantly bilateral and thalamo-cortical metabolic abnormalities, whereas tumor-associated epilepsy showed distinct metabolic alterations within tumors and the peritumoral zone. Treatment and prognostic studies demonstrated metabolite-specific changes following pharmacological and surgical interventions, and emerging metabolic MRI techniques provided complementary information on bioenergetics, ionic homeostasis, glutamatergic cycling, and metabolic flux. Conclusions: The available evidence supports epilepsy as a disorder of distributed metabolic networks that share a common signature of neuronal dysfunction while exhibiting syndrome-specific alterations in neurotransmission, gliosis, and energy metabolism. Complementary metabolic MRI techniques provide distinct biological information, but their clinical translation will require methodological harmonization and multimodal integration.

title: Endoscopic fenestration and Endoscope-Guided Placement of Ventriculoperitoneal Shunt with additional side holes for Multiloculated Hydrocephalus: A Technical Note
abstract: Abstract Multiloculated hydrocephalus (MLH) is characterized by multiple non-communicating cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) compartments and is associated with disproportionately high rates of shunt malfunction and revision surgery. We describe, in a stepwise technical format, an approach combining endoscopic cystoventriculostomy (inter-loculation fenestration) with endoscope-guided ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt catheter placement in an infant with multiloculated hydrocephalus. A 10-month-old male infant presented with progressive macrocephaly and developmental delay. Preoperative TORCH serology was notable for positive Rubella IgM and IgG, supporting a congenital rubella infection. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated multiple variable-sized loculated cysts (largest 30 × 39 mm) in the interhemispheric, bilateral parietal, and left temporal regions with mass effect on dilated lateral ventricles, in keeping with multiloculated hydrocephalus of probable post-infectious/congenital origin. A rigid neuroendoscope was used to sequentially fenestrate the intraventricular septa, and a single ventricular catheter, modified with additional side ports, was then advanced under direct endoscopic vision into the fenestrated common cavity. Wide endoscopic communication was established between the previously isolated loculations. A formal endoscopic third ventriculostomy was deliberately not attempted in this case because the distorted, loculated anatomy rendered safe access to the third ventricular floor unfavourable, compounded by the patient's young age and the extent of supratentorial multiloculation, which already necessitated shunt placement. The ventricular catheter tip and side holes were confirmed endoscopically to lie freely within the fenestrated cavity, away from choroid plexus and septal remnants, with free CSF drainage confirmed prior to closure. Postoperative CT confirmed marked decompression of the previously multiloculated cysts into a single residual cavity traversed by the catheter, without hemorrhage or new isolated loculation. Endoscopic fenestration combined with endoscope-guided, side-hole-modified catheter placement is a feasible and reproducible technique that allows direct, real-time confirmation of catheter position within a fenestrated common cavity. This may reduce the risk of isolated-compartment recurrence that complicates freehand or purely image-guided catheter placement in multiloculated hydrocephalus, although larger comparative series and longer follow-up are required.

title: CardioJEPA: A Framework for Holistic Cardiac Representations Through Predictive Multimodal Alignment with ECG-Preservation
abstract: Abstract The electrocardiogram (ECG) is the most widely used cardiac diagnostic tool, but it reflects cardiac structure and function only indirectly. Aligning ECG and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) representations offers a way to transfer imaging-derived structural knowledge into the ECG encoder without compromising the electrophysiological information it already carries. Contrastive learning has become the predominant approach for ECG--CMR alignment, yet the quality of the learned representation is jointly determined by the CMR target representation, the alignment objective, and the preservation of electrophysiological information unique to the ECG. We propose CardioJEPA, a predictive alignment framework built on frozen cardiac foundation models that addresses all three: a target that separates static anatomy from cardiac motion, a predictive objective that maps ECG representations onto a fixed CMR target without instance discrimination, and a preservation term that retains nearly all pre-alignment electrophysiological information. On 63,193 paired ECG--CMR recordings from the UK Biobank, CardioJEPA outperforms previous ECG--CMR alignment methods across structural, electrical, and diagnostic tasks, retains 98.6% of the ECG-unique information present before alignment, substantially reduces the modality gap relative to matched contrastive alignment, and transfers to external cohorts for structural heart disease and Chagas cardiomyopathy without task-specific training, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: Anatomically-Guided Attention for False Positive Reduction in Brain Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Abstract U-Net-based brain tumor segmentation can produce false positives in anatomically implausible locations, which inflate tumor volume estimates and reduce clinical trust. We investigate whether injecting an anatomical location prior into the network's attention can reduce these errors. We propose a prior informed attention gate that conditions U-Net features on empirical tumor-location prior maps computed from the training annotations, applied as a residual spatial gate at the bottleneck and at every decoder stage. Using the BRISC dataset of 2D contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI slices (glioma, meningioma and pituitary tumor), we compare the proposed model with a vanilla U-Net and a learned-gate ablation under identical training, using 3-fold cross-validation and a held-out test set of 860 images. We evaluate Dice, IoU, precision, recall, Hausdorff distance, HD95 and a dedicated far false-positive measure. The proposed model matched the baseline in Dice (0.709 versus 0.708) and showed a slightly lower but non-significant HD95 (36.5 versus 37.9 px, p = 0.26); it did not significantly reduce far false positives (49.7 versus 48.0 px, p = 0.82). A simple location prior injected through a spatial gate is therefore insufficient on BRISC, and stronger prior integration, longer training and additional datasets are needed to establish any benefit.

title: Successful Management of Acute SMV occlusion in Pancreatic Conversion Surgery After Carbon Ion Radiotherapy: A rare complication and surgical pitfall
abstract: Abstract Background: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is often locally advanced at diagnosis, and multimodal strategies including conversion therapy are used to increase the chance of margin-negative resection. Carbon-ion radiotherapy (CIRT) enables strong local tumor control. However, the side effect of CIRT toward local vasculature has not yet been fully understood. Literatures regarding the surgical pitfall of vessel reconstruction after CIRT have barely been reported. Case presentation: A 45-year-old female initially diagnosed with locally advanced PDAC underwent 14 cycles of systemic chemotherapy followed by CIRT. After conversion, she underwent distal pancreatectomy with common hepatic artery divestment. Superior mesenteric vein (SMV) was partially trimmed due to dense adhesion between pancreas, resulting in a 1.5cm defect. The defect was repaired primarily with 5 − 0 Prolene suture. On postoperative day2, she developed high fever and rapid deterioration of liver function. Urgent contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated critical narrowing/near-occlusion of portal vein/SMV without definite thrombus. Emergent exploratory laparotomy showed severe intimal fibrosis of SMV causing luminal compromise. The SMV defect was reconstructed using patch augmentation. The patient achieved an R0 resection with final pathological finding revealing residual ductal adenocarcinoma in a fibrotic background (pT1b pN0). Her Liver function rapidly recovered after the venous reconstruction. Conclusions: This case shows a rare post-CIRT vascular complication with SMV to portal vein fibrosis causing acute hepatic ischemia after pancreatic cancer conversion surgery, which was successfully rescued with prompt patch augmentation. To avoid such complications in conversion surgery for locally advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPC), it is of crucial importance to take radiation-related vasculopathy into consideration during the manipulation of vasculature nearby to the previously CIRT-radiated area.

title: Deep Learning-Based 3D Local Fibre Orientation Estimation in Composite Computed Tomography: From Volumetric Convolutions to Real-Time Direct Projection Inversion
abstract: Abstract The mechanical integrity, load-bearing efficiency, and damage tolerance of short- and continuous-fiber-reinforced polymer (SFRP/CFRP) composites depend intrinsically on their local 3D fiber-orientation distribution. While X-ray micro-computed tomography (μCT) non-destructively reveals microstructural morphology, standard volumetric extraction relies on classical 3D structure-tensor eigen-analysis. These classical approaches require dense angular projection sets (180+ views), computationally demanding Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) reconstructions, manual filter tuning, and exhibit severe degradation under Poisson photon noise. This paper introduces an end-to-end deep learning framework for local fiber orientation estimation that operates across two practical regimes: high-precision offline volumetric inspection and real-time inline scan-to-orientation inspection. To overcome the scarcity of physical CT ground truth, we develop a physics-grounded synthetic pipeline coupling directional sampling via the von Mises-Fisher (vMF) distribution (κ∈[0.5,25]) with collision-free Random Sequential Adsorption (RSA) packing (V_f∈[10%,35%]) and GPU-accelerated forward projection with realistic Poisson noise. Ground truth is formulated analytically through second-order orientation tensors, mathematically resolving the unoriented fiber director ±180^∘ sign ambiguity. We benchmark three paradigms across N=7,889 held-out sub-volume patches drawn from 150 independent composite phantoms (70/15/15 parent split): (1) classical 3D structure tensor eigen-analysis, (2) a 3D volumetric convolutional neural network (Model B), and (3) a novel Direct Projection Network (Model C) that infers 3D orientation directly from only 8 raw 2D sinogram projection views, completely bypassing 3D volumetric reconstruction. Model B achieves an overall mean angular error of 9.35 ∘ (4.78 ∘ on aligned tape; a 67% error reduction relative to the 28.27 ∘ classical baseline) at an inference throughput of 140.9 patches/s on GPU. Model C demonstrates that 3D orientation can be recovered directly from sparse 2D projection shadows with 22.57 ∘ overall error (11.35 ∘ on aligned composites), achieving 174.0 patches/s with zero reconstruction computational overhead. Furthermore, industrial tolerance evaluation demonstrates an 84.57% in-spec acceptance rate at automotive tolerance (τ≤15^∘) for Model B. This work demonstrates that deep learning provides both a superior offline alternative to classical image filtering and a viable pathway for inline, reconstruction-free composite manufacturing quality assurance.

title: AI-Based Particle Size Distribution Prediction from 3D Packed-Particle Tomographic Volumes: A Comparative Study with classical Watershed Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Abstract Determining the Particle Size Distribution (PSD) of granular media and powder compacts is vital across condensed matter physics, geological sciences, and materials engineering. While X-ray computed tomography (µCT) captures granular microstructure non-destructively, traditional quantitative PSD estimation relies on classical morphological segmentation (binarization, distance transform, and watershed flooding), which is computationally intensive and sensitive to contact-neck ambiguities. In this work, we investigate whether a compact 3D Convolutional Neural Network (Compact3DCNN, 300,900 parameters) can predict normalized 20-bin PSD histograms directly from unsegmented 3D grayscale volumes without intermediate particle instance extraction. Using a synthetic dataset of 60 independent non-overlapping polydisperse packed-sphere volumes (48 3 voxels) with exact analytic PSD ground truth, we benchmark the CNN against a classical 3D Euclidean distance-transform watershed baseline on an untouched, held-out test split (N = 10, 40 train / 10 validation / 10 test). On this low-to-moderate packing regime (15%–25%), the classical watershed baseline achieved superior accuracy, attaining a mean Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD) of 0.0974 ± 0.0261 voxels compared to 0.3428 ± 0.0949 voxels for the CNN (paired 95% bootstrap CI: [+0.1837, +0.3156] voxels). Measured runtime was 1.19 ± 0.27 ms per volume for the CNN on an NVIDIA RTX 3050 Laptop GPU versus 33.71 ± 7.50 ms for the watershed pipeline on an Intel CPU; however, we emphasize that this reflects disparate computing architectures rather than a controlled hardware comparison. title: A multicentre longitudinal brain metastasis imaging dataset with lesion segmentations and clinical data
abstract: Abstract Brain metastases exhibit substantial variability in lesion burden, morphology and treatment response. Longitudinal imaging linked to lesion annotations and clinical histories can support quantitative studies of this heterogeneity. We describe a multicentre dataset from seven Spanish hospitals comprising 443 patients diagnosed between 2007 and 2022, with follow-up imaging for 216 patients. The collection contains 2842 magnetic resonance image, including 1092 three dimensional (3D) contrast-enhanced T1-weighted, 833 T2-weighted and 917 FLAIR (fluid-attenuated inversion recovery) images. Semiautomatic 3D-segmentation with expert review provides annotations for 1291 unique lesions represented by 2303 lesion observations across imaging time points. Separate labels identify contrast-enhancing and non-enhancing or necrotic tumour components, and lesion identifiers are maintained during follow-up. Accompanying records describe primary tumour characteristics, treatments, imaging dates and clinical outcomes, together with acquisition metadata and 107 morphological and radiomic features. The dataset supports research on lesion detection and segmentation, longitudinal response assessment, imaging biomarkers and mathematical models of brain metastasis growth and treatment response.

title: CNN-Based Denoising of Industrial CT Images: A Residual-Learning Benchmark Against Classical Filters on Synthetic Phantoms
abstract: Abstract X-ray computed tomography (CT) lets engineers look inside manufactured parts without cutting them open. The catch is that the images are noisy, and the noise gets worse as the X-ray dose drops. That grain can hide the small pores and inclusions an inspector is actually looking for, and classical filters, which follow fixed rules, tend to blur the very edges they should protect. In this project, carried out with co-author Professor Mayank Goswami for course PHC-351 (Project 9, Category B), I built a fully synthetic, non-biological benchmark of 5,000 industrial phantoms (256 × 256 pixels). The phantoms have five outer shapes, bright rims, 0 to 6 dense inclusions and 0 to 9 pores, and the noise combines Poisson photon statistics with Gaussian electronic noise at three dose levels. I trained a 17-layer residual convolutional network (DnCNN, 556,096 parameters) on 4,200 images, validated it on 400, and compared it with Gaussian, median and non-local-means filters on 400 images it had never seen. DnCNN reached a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 50.28 dB and a structural similarity (SSIM) of 0.998. For comparison, non-local means scored 45.56 dB and 0.910, the median filter 41.38 dB and 0.964, the Gaussian filter 37.44 dB and 0.857, and the noisy input 37.93 dB and 0.809. DnCNN beat the best classical filter on all 400 test images (smallest margin + 1.87 dB, mean + 4.72 dB) and at every dose level (low 48.92 dB, medium 50.06 dB, high 50.88 dB). One caveat matters: training and test noise come from the same simulator, so these numbers are a best case, and testing on real scanner data is the obvious next step.

title: Deep Volumetric Classification of Pore Morphology in 3D Micro-Computed Tomography of Additively Manufactured Metallic Components
abstract: Abstract Internal porosity represents a critical factor governing mechanical fatigue and failure in metal additive manufacturing (AM). In fracture mechanics, void geometry dictates local stress intensity factors; acute and elongated geometries concentrate mechanical stress significantly more than spherical voids. Consequently, automated categorization of volumetric defects into Spherical, Elongated, and Irregular morphologies from 3D X-ray micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) is essential for non-destructive evaluation. Due to experimental acquisition constraints and extreme class imbalance in physical scans (837 labeled voids: 6.45% spherical, 44.80% elongated, 48.75% irregular), we developed a procedural 3D synthetic pore generation framework to train deep convolutional architectures. While an initial 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D CNN) achieved 99.89% validation accuracy on synthetic data, zero-shot transfer on physical scans collapsed completely to the elongated class due to detector attenuation polarity inversion and a large-void size cutoff. Recalibrating synthetic data with scanner point-spread function (PSF) blur, noise, and sub-voxel micro-radii yielded 97.83% synthetic accuracy, yet exhibited a secondary mode collapse on physical scans due to ambient background air saturation along hollow tube boundaries. Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) diagnostics identified an order-of-magnitude volume scale mismatch between synthetic models (mean 67.51 voxels) and real defects (mean 6.76 voxels). A controlled 5-experiment ablation benchmark (Exp A–E) on a locked real held-out test set (N = 126, seed = 42) demonstrated that synthetic pretraining yielded no performance gain (42.86%) relative to training from scratch on physical scans (45.24%). Conversely, a classical Random Forest trained on mathematical geometric descriptors achieved 99.21% accuracy, confirming ground-truth label separability and establishing that raw-voxel 3D CNNs are fundamentally constrained by spatial discretization limits (53.6 μm/voxel). We propose a hybrid multi-modal feature fusion architecture bridging raw volumetric representations with classical geometric invariants for robust industrial deployment.

title: Autoencoder–Graph Neural Network Framework for Robust 3D Pore Connectivity Classification in Noisy Volumetric Images
abstract: Abstract Pore connectivity is a critical property governing the transport of fluids, gases, and ions in porous materials. Connectivity is often inferred from micro-computed tomography (μCT) volumes through thresholding and connected-component analysis. However, this pipeline is sensitive to noise and limited resolution, producing both false connections and missed links. This study investigates whether graph-based learning, using geometric features and 3D image representations, can correct such errors. We generate 250 synthetic 128³-voxel phantoms with known ground-truth connectivity, degrade them using point-spread blur and noise, and evaluate ten models spanning classical machine learning, 3D CNNs, GCN, GraphSAGE, and autoencoder–GNN fusion. The best-performing models (GraphSAGE and AE+GraphSAGE) achieve F1 scores of 0.954 and 0.957, respectively, compared with 0.468 for the raw connected-component baseline. Improvements are driven primarily by geometric features, including neck width, centroid distance, and pore volume, while frozen autoencoder embeddings provide negligible benefit. However, improved edge classification does not consistently translate into better cluster agreement or percolation prediction.

title: Sharp but Wrong? Fidelity and Hallucination in Deep CT Super-Resolution with Analytic Phantoms
abstract: Abstract Deep super-resolution (SR) techniques could potentially recover the resolution that X-ray computed tomography (CT) sacrifices to reduce radiation dose and scanning time. However, in CT imaging, generating details that appear plausible but are not physically present represents a critical failure that standard evaluation metrics cannot detect.In this study, we train two deep-learning models to upsample CT slices: a pixel-loss residual network (EDSR) and an adversarially trained network (ESRGAN). Both models are evaluated in terms of reconstruction fidelity and their tendency to hallucinate image details.To assess hallucinated details, we use analytical phantoms containing line-pair gratings and pores with precisely known frequencies and diameters. The evaluation includes held-out frequency bands, a documented blur–decimation–noise model, and a validated spectral measurement method that classifies each grating as resolved, washed out, aliased, or hallucinated.At ×4 upscaling, all neural networks improve PSNR by more than 6 dB compared with bicubic and Lanczos interpolation. ESRGAN achieves the best perceptual score (LPIPS = 0.015 compared with 0.046 for EDSR), at the cost of approximately 2 dB in reconstruction fidelity. However, ESRGAN hallucinates 61% of the gratings that cannot be represented in the input image, whereas interpolation methods produce no hallucinated gratings.An adversarial-weight sweep demonstrates that perceptual loss alone is responsible for these invented details. Pixel-loss networks also exhibit limitations, replacing held-out gratings just below the Nyquist limit with their aliased counterparts learned during training.At ×2 upscaling, hallucination rates decrease substantially but do not disappear entirely, with ESRGAN still hallucinating 27% of the gratings. Interestingly, pores and thin lines that were never encountered during training are successfully recovered by all networks.All experimental data are synthetic and reproducible using a specified random seed.

title: Segmentation-Free Estimation of Fibre, Matrix and Void Fractions from Simulated X-ray CT of Fibre Composites with a 3D Residual Network
abstract: Abstract Fibre volume fraction and void content govern the stiffness and interlaminar strength of fibre-reinforced polymers, but measuring them from X-ray computed tomography (CT) normally requires voxel-wise segmentation, which is fragile when carbon fibre and epoxy differ little in attenuation and when fibres are only a few voxels across. We instead regress the three volume fractions of a CT sub-volume directly using a 3D residual network (3.6 million parameters, with a softmax output ensuring that the fractions sum to one). Training and test data are simulated: 66 synthetic composites with fibre contents ranging from 40% to 66% and void contents ranging from 0% to 5% are generated on a supersampled grid, ensuring that every crop has exact ground truth. The composites are scanned using a physics-based CT simulator incorporating parallel-beam projection, Poisson noise at three dose levels, detector blur, and filtered back-projection. On 216 test crops from 9 held-out composites, the network achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.84 percentage points (pp) [95% confidence interval: 0.66–1.05] for fibre and 0.17 pp [0.11–0.25] for void, compared with 6.06 pp and 0.28 pp, respectively, for the best threshold- or histogram-based methods. The network is more accurate on all 9 test composites for fibre and matrix (Wilcoxon p = 0.0039, the minimum attainable value for n = 9). Its fibre error increases only from 0.69 to 1.07 pp as the contrast-to-noise ratio decreases from 5.2 to 1.2. For void estimation, the network does not significantly outperform a Gaussian-mixture histogram fit (p = 0.36) and tends to overestimate void content below 1%. A mean-grey-value estimator calibrated on validation data achieves comparable performance (1.09 vs 0.87 pp; p = 0.20). However, a 2% calibration error increases its estimation error to 8.4 pp, whereas the network, whose input is normalized independently for each crop, remains completely unaffected.

title: Connected vs. Isolated Pore Classification via Learned Refinement of Connected-Component Analysis
abstract: Abstract The classification of isolated versus interconnected pores in porous media is critical for structural and fatigue assessments, yet classical 26-connectivity connected-component (CC) labeling fails catastrophically under realistic computed tomography (CT) noise due to the formation of false artifact webs. This study proposes a two-stage machine learning refinement pipeline to correct classical thresholding errors. Following Watershed over-segmentation to generate a proposal graph, we extract handcrafted geometric features—specifically minimum neck radius and path intensity—which successfully separate physical bridges from disconnected noise. We evaluate an XGBoost classifier, a GraphSAGE Graph Neural Network (GNN), and a 3D-CNN against the unrefined CC baseline. Feature importance analysis confirms that the tree-based model anchors its predictions on true physical geometry rather than random noise. While Watershed over-segmentation causes localized false-split penalties under the global Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), the learned refinement models achieve robust edge-level connectivity classification (Validation F1 ≥ 0.94), successfully severing the noise-induced bridge artifacts that compromise classical 26-connectivity thresholding.

title: When Near-Perfect Accuracy Is a Warning Sign: Frame-Level Data Leakage in 3D CNN Classification of the Alzheimer's Disease Spectrum from fMRI Volumes
abstract: Abstract Deep learning studies on neuroimaging data frequently report accuracies close to 100%, yet such results can arise from data leakage rather than from learned disease signal. This paper is a case study of that failure in the author’s own work. A 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) was trained to separate Alzheimer’s disease (AD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), early MCI (EMCI) and cognitively normal (CN) participants using 191,428 individual 3D volumes extracted from functional MRI (fMRI) acquisitions in the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). Each time frame was treated as an independent image, and the pooled frames were split at random, at the image level, into training and validation sets. The network reached 100% validation accuracy by epoch 14 and made no errors on any of the 191,428 volumes. We show that this outcome is explained by frame-level leakage: frames of the same participant are nearly identical, so a model can recognise individuals instead of disease stages, and a random split places almost every participant on both sides. We document the training signatures that exposed the problem, relate them to leakage patterns reported in the Alzheimer’s literature, quantify why image-level splitting of fMRI frames guarantees subject overlap, and propose a subject-level evaluation protocol. The corrected experiment is left to future work; the contribution of this paper is a transparent, reproducible account of how a plausible pipeline yields an invalid result, and how to detect it.

title: A Multiscale Biophysical Reaction-Diffusion Framework Coupling Histological Architecture, Interstitial Transport, and Inflammatory Tension in Solid Tumors: An Exploratory In Silico and Retrospective Multi-Cohort Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background In solid oncology, anatomical TNM staging and somatic mutational profiling provide the cornerstone of clinical risk stratification. Nevertheless, substantial clinical heterogeneity remains unexplained: curatively resected (R0) tumors frequently recur, and targeted adjuvant therapies—such as 36-month adjuvant osimertinib in the landmark ADAURA trial—exhibit a post-discontinuation recurrence rebound where 67.9% of all relapse events occur after planned treatment cessation. Similarly, in desmoplastic colorectal cancer (CMS4 subtype), cytotoxic chemotherapy de-escalation/escalation strategies (investigated in trials such as PEGASUS) confront persistent micrometastatic reservoirs that evade clearance. We hypothesized that post-resection persistence and delayed relapse are modulated by the biophysical coupling between epithelial polarity integrity (“The Seed”) and microenvironmental inflammatory-transport resistance (“The Soil”). Methods We established a multiscale biophysical reaction-diffusion continuum model integrating: 1. Spatial drug penetration across microvascular cords governed by modified cylindrical Bessel functions of the second kind (K0); 2. Interstitial transport limitations driven by elevated interstitial fluid pressure ( I F P ≈ 20 – 35 mmHg) and absent functional lymphatic drainage (Δ P ≈ 0); 3. Plastic drug-tolerant persister (DTP) cell transitions within viable, sub-therapeutic annular niches (p O2 ≥ 1 – 2 mmHg); 4. A hereditary Volterra memory functional of residual cytotoxic immune surveillance (Eimm ( t ) = E0 e− γ ∫ Φ d τ) formalizing cumulative inflammatory damage; 5. An exploratory translational metric—the Host-Tumor Biophysical Index (HTBI)—integrating histopathological polarity, stromal desmoplasia, and systemic inflammatory blood parameters (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio [NLR] and C-reactive protein [CRP]). In accordance with REMARK reporting recommendations, the framework was evaluated across 3,461 curatively treated cancer patients with clinically indexed records across 11 cohorts (with 3,425 complete matched multi-omic and blood profiles analyzed, strictly excluding 36 TCGA cases lacking paired RNA-seq matrices and 274 incomplete blood records): - Discovery Cohort: 604 curatively resected lung adenocarcinoma patients from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC 2020); - Raw Blood Chemistry Cohort: 1,056 curatively resected surgical patients evaluated via strict complete-case analysis with raw pre-operative complete blood counts (NLR) and serum CRP/Albumin (PLOS ONE open data); - Multi-Cohort Solid Epithelial Cohorts (N = 986 matched RNA-seq / N =1 ,222 clinical): Colorectal (TCGA-COADREAD, N =592), Pancreatic (TCGA-PAAD, N =177), Esophageal (TCGA-ESCA, N =181), Cholangiocarcinoma (TCGA-CHOL, N =36), and External Lung (GSE31210, N = 226); - Inherited Cholangiopathy Model: 18 clinically annotated biliary cases (JAG1, NOTCH2, PKHD1, TJP2); - Proof-by-Contradiction Falsification Controls (N =535): Acute Myeloid Leukemia (TCGA-LAML, N =149), Testicular Germ Cell (TCGA-TGCT, N =133), and Soft-Tissue Sarcoma (TCGA-SARC, N = 253); - External Clinical Trial Anchor: The landmark double-blind randomized CANTOS trial (The Lancet 2017, N =10 ,061). Findings In the complete-case raw laboratory cohort (N =1 ,056), pre-operative biophysical inflammatory tier stratified 5-year overall survival from 69.4% (Low HTBI) to 56.7% (High HTBI) (p =3.81×10−7), maintaining independent prognostic association in multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression adjusting for Pathologic TNM Stage and Histological Grade (Hazard Ratio H R =1.43, 95 %CI:1.14 – 1.81 , p = 0.0022; continuous multivariable H R = 2.20, p = 0.00041). In the MSKCC lung adenocarcinoma discovery cohort (N = 604 , 98 recurrences), continuous decoupled HTBI conferred an adjusted H R = 2.49 ( 95 %CI:1.00 – 6.18 , p = 0.050) (binary adjusted H R =1.89, p = 0.029) after controlling for Pathologic TNM Stage (H R = 2.53 , p < 0.0005), patient sex, and somatic EGFR mutations. Schoenfeld residuals confirmed proportional hazards ( χ2 =3.82 , p = 0.431). 500-fold bootstrap cross-validation showed an incremental discrimination gain (ΔC -index =+ 0.050 , p = 0.044; 2-year A U C = 0.794). title: Multi-Class Gastric Histopathology Classification Using a Hybrid Swin Transformer–ConvNeXt Model
abstract: Abstract Diagnosing gastric cancer still depends, for the most part, on a pathologist looking at stained tissue slides under a microscope. The disease kills roughly 660{,}000 people every year, and although early detection makes a real difference to survival, manual slide reading is slow and two experts examining the same slide do not always agree. In this work we built a system that tries to ease that burden. We trained a hybrid deep learning model on the Gastric Cancer Histopathology Tissue Image Dataset (GCHTID), pairing a Swin Transformer, which is good at picking up the broad structural layout of a tissue patch, with a ConvNeXt network, which captures the fine local textures where early malignant changes tend to hide. Every image first passes through a simple preprocessing chain of median filtering and CLAHE contrast enhancement, a combination we settled on after comparing several denoising and enhancement options. The ensemble sorts each patch into one of eight classes: tumor tissue (TUM) plus seven benign types-adipose, debris, lymphocytes, mucus, smooth muscle, normal mucosa, and stroma. On held-out data it reached 75.35% test accuracy (88.76% training, 76.99% best validation), beating the single-model baselines we tried, including ViT and EfficientNet-B3. To make the model usable outside a notebook, we wrapped it in a Flask REST API and a small web interface where a user can upload a slide image, see the prediction and its confidence, download a PDF report, and look back through past results. The system is a research prototype rather than a clinical tool, but the results suggest that combining transformer and convolutional features is a workable direction for computer-assisted pathology.

title: AI-Based Interfacial Contact Area Prediction in 3D Granular Media: Benchmarking Volumetric CNN, GNN, and Classical Surface Meshing
abstract: Abstract Interfacial contact area between contiguous grains governs macroscopic elastic moduli, stress transmission chains, effective thermal and electrical conductivity, and solid-state diffusion rates in three-dimensional (3D) granular media. Standard characterization of X-ray micro-computed tomography (µCT) volumes relies on 3D Euclidean distance transform seeding and marker-controlled watershed segmentation followed by polygonal surface extraction via the Marching-Cubes algorithm (Lorensen & Cline, 1987). However, Cartesian voxelization introduces severe staircase terracing along curved inter-particle boundaries, inflating surface area measurements by 40% to 80%, while local mesh triangulation scales poorly to assemblies containing thousands of grains. Conducted under the supervision of Prof. Mayank Goswami , this study establishes a comparative benchmark of four data-driven surrogate architectures—an interpretable Random Forest ensemble, a 4-block 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D CNN) operating on 48 3 binary dual-particle patches, a 3-layer bidirectional GraphSAGE Graph Neural Network (GNN) operating on the global contact graph G = (V, E) , and a multimodal Hybrid GNN + CNN fusion architecture—across 250 synthetic 3D granular phantoms (50,800 particles and 48,750 contact interfaces). Across 38 held-out test specimens (7,466 contact interfaces), we evaluate models under both DEM-coupled (known sphere geometry) and blind tomographic (voxel-only, zero metadata) operating regimes. When coupled with exact inter-particle distance and radius attributes, the 3-layer bidirectional GraphSAGE network achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.158 vx 2 , a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.217 vx 2 , a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 1.91% , and R 2 = 0.99999 at an inference latency of 2.89 ms per phantom , while the Random Forest baseline achieves R 2 = 0.99992 and MAE = 0.409 vx 2 . Crucially, an explicit feature-circularity ablation study demonstrates that removing pairwise distance and overlap features collapses tabular/graph accuracy to R 2 = 0.4387 (MAE = 44.68 vx 2 ), proving that inter-centroid geometry is physically indispensable; however, estimating these quantities 100% blindly from watershed-segmented voxels via principal inertia axes ( R̂ i = L maj,i /2, MAE = 0.048 vx) restores R 2 = 0.9959 (MAE = 3.35 vx 2 ) without ground-truth metadata. Furthermore, the purely image-based 4-block 3D CNN —which requires zero tabular or metadata inputs—achieves R 2 = 0.99788 and MAE = 2.434 vx 2 (166.23 ms/phantom), outperforming classical Marching-Cubes surface meshing (MAE = 42.750 vx 2 , MAPE = 72.24%, R 2 = 0.50471, 3,555.60 ms/phantom) by 17.6× in accuracy and 21.4× in speed. Scaling experiments up to N = 2,000 particles, overlap-depth stratification, per-particle contact area aggregation ( n = 6,879 active test grains), and domain adaptation to mildly non-spherical superellipsoids (3D CNN R 2 = 0.9979, MAE = 2.50 vx 2 ) establish practical guidelines, methodological limitations, and ethical safeguards for deploying AI surrogates in granular mechanics.

title: Bottleneck Width, Loss Design and the Limits of Skip-Free Convolutional Denoising Autoencoders for Simulated Low-Dose CT
abstract: Abstract Convolutional denoising autoencoders (DAEs) are attractive for computed tomography (CT) because they offer a small model and a compact, reusable latent code, but it is unclear whether a skip-free DAE can compete with feed-forward residual networks. We examine this question on 41 abdominal CT volumes from the Medical Segmentation Decathlon (820 real slices, split by volume) and 300 synthetic multi-material phantoms, corrupted with a two-stage noise model (Poisson photon noise followed by Gaussian read noise). We train convolutional DAEs with bottleneck widths of 8 to 256 channels, a variational variant and a composite MSE+SSIM loss, and compare them with a DnCNN-style network and with Gaussian, median and non-local-means filters on identical held-out volumes. DnCNN reached 44.21 dB PSNR and 0.979 SSIM, against 35.07 dB and 0.938 for the best MSE-trained autoencoder; the noisy input scored 35.56 dB and 0.756. The composite loss raised the autoencoder to 35.65 dB and 0.950. Quality was flat between 32 and 256 channels (PSNR spread 0.22 dB) and dropped only at 16 and 8 channels (− 0.9 and − 2.5 dB relative to width 128). On real slices the width-128 autoencoder lowered PSNR relative to the noisy input in 71% of cases, mainly at thin, high-contrast structures, even though SSIM improved by about 0.12. Latent codes predicted phantom material with 66–84% accuracy (chance 20%) but formed no clusters (silhouette ≈ 0). The autoencoder needed about 34 times less compute per tile than DnCNN, yet was far less accurate. In this setting the reconstruction-through-a-bottleneck design, rather than bottleneck size, appears to limit denoising quality; the role of skip connections remains to be isolated.
